q.s: Which of the following statements about the periods of Mehrgarh is correct?
o: Period I was an aceramic Neolithic phase with mud-brick houses.
Copper working begins in Period I.
Pottery first appears in Period I.
Wheel-made painted pottery appears in Period II.
q.x: Period I was aceramic; pottery and cotton appear in Period II and copper working with wheel-made painted pottery in Period III.

q.s: In Harappan towns, the house drains usually emptied into:
o: Open fields outside the town wall
q.x: House drains joined covered street drains provided with manholes, and waste water finally went into soak pits or main channels.

q.s: Which of the following Harappan sites is noted for NOT having a systematic drainage system?
q.x: Banawali lacked the systematic drainage seen in most Harappan towns; at Lothal the houses were of mud brick but the drains of burnt brick.

q.s: The view that the Harappan script records a Proto-Dravidian language is associated with:
q.x: Iravatham Mahadevan, Asko Parpola and Father Heras hold the most supported Proto-Dravidian view; S. R. Rao read the script as Indo-Aryan.

q.s: Which of the following scholars did NOT read the Harappan script as Proto-Dravidian?
q.x: S. R. Rao read the script as Indo-Aryan (Sanskritic); Mahadevan, Parpola and Heras support the Proto-Dravidian view.

q.s: The largest of the Brahmanas, which tells the story of the Great Flood and the eastward journey of Videgha Madhava, is:
q.x: The Shatapatha Brahmana (Shukla Yajurveda) is the largest Brahmana and records the Flood story and Videgha Madhava's eastward migration.

q.s: The first literary mention of the Andhras is found in the:
q.x: The Aitareya Brahmana of the Rig Veda first mentions the Andhras, describing them as descendants of Vishwamitra's sons.

q.s: During the Second Urbanisation in the Ganga plain, forest clearance and agricultural surplus were made possible mainly by:
q.x: Iron tools helped clear the Ganga plain forests and produce a surplus; trade and coinage then allowed taxes and wages to be paid in money.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT associated with the Second Urbanisation in the Ganga valley?
q.x: NBPW, punch-marked coins and iron tools mark the Second Urbanisation (c. 600 BCE); seals belong to the Harappan (first) urbanisation.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an element of stupa architecture?
q.x: Medhi (drum), torana (gateway) and chhatra (umbrella) are stupa parts; the shikhara is the spire of a Hindu temple.

q.s: The path for clockwise circumambulation round a stupa is called:
q.x: Devotees walk clockwise round the stupa along the pradakshinapatha; the vedika is the railing and the anda the hemispherical dome.

q.s: The Jain term 'Tirthankara' literally means:
q.x: A Tirthankara is a 'ford-maker' who shows the crossing over the ocean of rebirth; 'Jina' means conqueror.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a Jain Tirthankara?
q.x: Makkhali Gosala founded the Ajivika sect; Rishabhadeva was the first, Neminatha the 22nd and Parshvanatha the 23rd Tirthankara.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a Jain doctrine?
q.x: Shunyavada is the Buddhist Madhyamika doctrine of Nagarjuna; Anekantavada (many-sidedness), Syadvada and Nayavada are Jain.

q.s: Kundakundacharya, author of the Samayasara and Pravachanasara, belonged to which Jain sect?
q.x: Kundakundacharya was a Digambara monk; the Ajivikas were a separate sect founded by Makkhali Gosala.

q.s: The doctrine of niyati (fate) was the central teaching of:
q.x: Niyati, absolute determinism, was taught by Makkhali Gosala of the Ajivikas; Ajita Kesakambalin was a materialist.

q.s: The Mauryan emperor Bindusara ruled during the period:
q.x: Bindusara (birth name Simhasena, mother Durdhara) ruled c. 297-273 BCE between Chandragupta and Ashoka.

q.s: Which Seleucid ruler sent sweet wine and dried figs to Bindusara but refused to send a philosopher?
q.x: Antiochus I Soter sent the wine and figs but replied that Greeks did not sell philosophers.

q.s: The identification of 'Sandrocottus' of the Greek accounts with Chandragupta Maurya was first made by:
q.x: Sir William Jones made the identification in 1793; James Prinsep later deciphered the Brahmi script (1837).

q.s: After the Kalinga War, Ashoka replaced Bherighosha (the sound of the war drum) with:
q.x: Ashoka gave up conquest by arms; Bherighosha gave way to Dhammaghosha and Dhammavijaya replaced military conquest.

q.s: According to Jain tradition, Chandragupta Maurya spent his last days at Shravanabelagola along with:
q.x: Chandragupta followed the Jain teacher Bhadrabahu to Shravanabelagola, where he is said to have died by sallekhana.

q.s: Which of the following was a feature of the late Gupta period?
o: Large issues of silver punch-marked coins
Gold coins with less gold and more alloy
Spread of Gupta rule into Saurashtra
q.x: Later Gupta gold coins were debased with more alloy, and money payments were slowly replaced by land grants; Gupta coins disappear from western Malwa and Saurashtra after Skandagupta.

q.s: The titles 'Shakraditya' and 'Mahendraditya' were borne by the Gupta ruler:
q.x: Kumaragupta I bore these titles and was a devotee of Kartikeya (peacock-type coins); Chandragupta II was a Vaishnava (Paramabhagavata).

q.s: Which of the following titles was NOT borne by Kumaragupta I?
q.x: Baladitya was the title of the later Gupta ruler Narasimhagupta; Kumaragupta I bore Shakraditya, Mahendraditya and Ajitamahendra.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the Gram Sabha?
q.x: Article 243A provides for the Gram Sabha; 243B for the three tiers, 243D for reservation and 243E for the five-year term.

q.s: Reservation of not less than one-third of seats for women in Panchayats is provided under:
q.x: Article 243D provides for reservation of seats for SCs, STs and not less than one-third for women; 243G deals with powers of Panchayats.

q.s: The Kallanai (Grand Anicut) across the Kaveri is attributed to:
q.x: The Grand Anicut is credited to the Sangam Chola king Karikala, not to the imperial Cholas.

q.s: The Delhi Sultan who introduced the silver tanka and the copper jital was:
q.x: Iltutmish issued the standard Arabic coins, the silver tanka and copper jital, and received investiture from the Abbasid Caliph in 1229.

q.s: Nasiruddin Qabacha, a rival of Iltutmish, held power over:
q.x: Qabacha ruled Multan and Uch; Iltutmish defeated Tajuddin Yildiz at Tarain in 1216. Badaun was Iltutmish's own early iqta.

q.s: Timur invaded India in 1398 during the reign of:
q.x: Timur's invasion came in 1398 under Nasiruddin Mahmud Tughlaq, after Firoz's death; Khizr Khan later founded the Sayyid dynasty.

q.s: The Sayyid dynasty of Delhi was founded by:
q.x: Khizr Khan, Timur's nominee, founded the Sayyid dynasty in 1414, ending the Tughlaq period (1320-1414).

q.s: Ziauddin Barani set out his ideal of kingship in the work:
q.x: Barani wrote the Fatawa-i-Jahandari on statecraft (and the Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi); the Tabaqat-i-Nasiri is by Minhaj-us-Siraj.

q.s: Under the Delhi Sultanate, religious grants were looked after by the:
q.x: The Sadr-us-Sudur managed religious grants and affairs; the Qazi-ul-Quzat was the chief judge.

q.s: Kalhana's Rajatarangini, the chronicle of Kashmir, is divided into:
q.x: Kalhana's Rajatarangini (12th century) is divided into eight tarangas (waves).

q.s: 'Madhura Vijayam', describing the conquest of the Madurai Sultanate by Kumara Kampana, was written by:
q.x: Gangadevi, Kampana's wife, wrote Madhura Vijayam, which describes conditions in Madurai under the Sultanate.

q.s: The First Battle of Panipat (1526) was fought between Babur and:
q.x: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat in 1526, the first large-scale use of field artillery in North India; Rana Sanga was defeated at Khanwa (1527).

q.s: Which of the following battles was NOT fought by Babur?
q.x: Babur fought Panipat I (1526), Khanwa (1527), Chanderi (1528) and Ghaghra (1529); Panipat II (1556) was fought by Akbar's forces against Hemu.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of Sher Shah's land revenue system?
q.x: The Dahsala (ten-year average) system was introduced by Akbar through Todar Mal; patta, qabuliyat and jaribana belonged to Sher Shah's system.

q.s: Under Sher Shah, 'jaribana' was the fee paid to the:
q.x: Jaribana was the surveyor's fee and muhasilana the collector's fee.

q.s: Under Akbar's land revenue system, the state's share of the average produce was fixed at:
q.x: Under the Zabti system the state took one-third of the average produce, paid in cash (dams); land was measured with the Gaz-i-Ilahi and a bamboo jarib.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT part of Akbar's land revenue system?
q.x: The iqta was the Delhi Sultanate's revenue assignment; Zabti, Dahsala and the Gaz-i-Ilahi were features of Akbar's system.

q.s: The Persian governor who surrendered Kandahar to Shah Jahan in 1638 was:
q.x: Ali Mardan Khan surrendered Kandahar in 1638; Persia took it back in 1649 and later Mughal sieges failed.

q.s: Which Mughal prince led the unsuccessful siege of Kandahar in 1653?
q.x: Aurangzeb's sieges (1649, 1652) and Dara Shikoh's siege (1653) all failed, and Kandahar was lost for good.

q.s: The tomb of Sher Shah at Sasaram, set in a tank, is regarded as marking the transition from:
o: The Lodi style to the Mughal style
The Tughlaq style to the Lodi style
The Mughal style to the Rajput style
The Khalji style to the Tughlaq style
q.x: Sher Shah's tomb at Sasaram links the Lodi style to the Mughal style.

q.s: Which of the following statements about medieval tombs is correct?
o: The tomb of Itimad-ud-Daula is the first Mughal tomb built wholly of white marble.
Sher Shah's tomb at Sasaram is built wholly of white marble.
The first true arch appears in the tomb of Sikandar Lodi.
The tomb of Itimad-ud-Daula was built by Jahangir.
q.x: Nur Jahan built the white-marble tomb of Itimad-ud-Daula; the first true arch is in Balban's tomb, Sikandar Lodi's tomb has the first double dome, and Sher Shah's tomb is of sandstone.

q.s: Who among the following is known as the 'Pitamaha of Carnatic music'?
q.x: Purandara Dasa, a disciple of Vyasa Tirtha, systematised the teaching of Carnatic music and is called its Pitamaha.

q.s: The Dvaita teacher who spread Madhva's philosophy in Andhra-Kalinga from Srikurmam was:
q.x: Narahari Tirtha worked from Srikurmam; Vyasa Tirtha wrote the Nyayamrita and Tarka Tandava.

q.s: The Sufi doctrine of Wahdat-ul-Wujud (Unity of Being) is associated with:
q.x: Ibn Arabi's Wahdat-ul-Wujud holds Haq (Creator) and Khalq (creation) are one; Sirhindi opposed it with Wahdat-ush-Shuhud.

q.s: Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi, who propounded Wahdat-ush-Shuhud, belonged to the:
q.x: Sirhindi was a Naqshbandi saint, known as Mujaddid-i-Alf-i-Sani.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a factor in the rise of the Marathas?
o: The influence of the Bhakti saints
Strengthening of Mughal finances by the Deccan war
Maratha service in Bijapur and Ahmadnagar
q.x: Aurangzeb's 27-year Deccan war drained Mughal finances; the terrain, Bhakti saints and administrative experience under the Deccan sultanates aided the Marathas.

q.s: The Nawab of Awadh deposed at the time of the annexation of Awadh in 1856 was:
q.x: Wajid Ali Shah was deposed by Dalhousie in 1856 on grounds of misgovernment and exiled to Calcutta (Metiabruz).

q.s: The Summary Revenue Settlement of 1856 in Awadh was made directly with the:
q.x: The 1856 settlement set aside the taluqdars and dealt with village proprietors; the taluqdars were also disarmed.

q.s: The Battle of Chandurti (Condore), 1758, which drove the French out of the Northern Circars, was fought near:
q.x: Chandurti near Rajahmundry (1758), called by Malleson "a small battle with great results", gave the English their first foothold in the Northern Circars.

q.s: The British Governor-General during the Third Anglo-Mysore War, who led the campaign in person, was:
q.x: Cornwallis led the Third War (1790-92) in person; Hastings presided over the Second and Wellesley the Fourth (1799).

q.s: Which of the following Governors-General was NOT associated with any of the Anglo-Mysore Wars?
q.x: Hastings (Second), Cornwallis (Third) and Wellesley (Fourth) were linked with the Mysore Wars; Dalhousie came half a century later (1848-56).

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a term of the Treaty of Seringapatam (1792)?
o: Tipu ceded about half his territory
Tipu gave two sons as hostages
Tipu paid a war indemnity of Rs 3 crore
q.x: Tipu never accepted a subsidiary alliance; in 1792 he ceded half his territory, paid Rs 3 crore and gave two sons as hostages.

q.s: Under the Regulating Act of 1773, the Governor-General of Bengal had:
o: Only a casting vote in his council
An absolute veto over his council
q.x: Decisions were by majority of the council of four; the Governor-General had only a casting vote, so Hastings was often outvoted by Francis, Clavering and Monson.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a member of the Governor-General's Council under the Regulating Act, 1773?
q.x: The council of four was Francis, Clavering, Monson and Barwell; Elijah Impey was the first Chief Justice of the Supreme Court at Calcutta.

q.s: The Hartog Committee (1929) on education was appointed during the viceroyalty of:
q.x: The Hartog Committee came under Irwin; the Sadler Commission was under Chelmsford and the Sargent Plan (1944) under Wavell.

q.s: Which of the following commissions was NOT appointed during the viceroyalty of Lord Curzon?
q.x: The Hunter Commission (1882) came under Ripon; the Universities Commission (1902), the Police Commission (1902) and the Irrigation Commission (1901) were Curzon's.

q.s: After the 1937 provincial elections, the Unionist ministry in Punjab was headed by:
q.x: Sikandar Hayat Khan led the Unionist ministry; Fazlul Huq headed Bengal and Allah Baksh Sindh.

q.s: After the 1937 elections, in which of the following provinces did the Congress NOT form the ministry?
q.x: Punjab had a Unionist ministry under Sikandar Hayat Khan; the Congress formed ministries in Bombay (B.G. Kher), Madras (Rajaji) and Orissa.

q.s: The Atheist Centre founded by Gora at Mudunuru in 1940 was later shifted to:
q.x: Gora founded the Atheist Centre at Mudunuru in 1940 and moved it to Vijayawada in 1947; he wrote 'Positive Atheism'.

q.s: Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary, the rationalist writer and Chairman of the Tenali Municipality, was popularly known as:
q.x: Tripuraneni Ramaswamy was called 'Kavi Raju'; his song 'Veeragandham techinamu' is linked with the Civil Disobedience Movement.

q.s: Who presided over the first Provincial Panchama Mahajana Sabha?
q.x: Bhagya Reddy Varma presided over the Sabha, which was organised by Guduru Ramachandra Rao.

q.s: The Vaikom Satyagraha (1924-25) was launched for the right of lower castes to:
o: Use the roads around the Vaikom temple
Enter the sanctum of Guruvayur temple
q.x: Led by T.K. Madhavan, K.P. Kesava Menon and K. Kelappan, it sought use of the roads around the Vaikom temple; the Temple Entry Proclamation came only in 1936.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT among the leaders of the Vaikom Satyagraha?
q.x: T.K. Madhavan, K.P. Kesava Menon and K. Kelappan led the Vaikom Satyagraha; Gandhi visited in 1925 to negotiate a compromise.

q.s: Ayyankali of Kerala founded the:
q.x: Ayyankali founded the Sadhu Jana Paripalana Sangham; the Adi-Hindu Social Service League and Jagan Mitra Mandali were Bhagya Reddy Varma's, and the Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha Ambedkar's.

q.s: Which of the following organisations was NOT founded by Bhagya Reddy Varma?
q.x: The Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha (1924) was founded by Ambedkar; Bhagya Reddy Varma founded the Jagan Mitra Mandali, Manya Sangham and Adi-Hindu Social Service League.

q.s: In the first elections under the Montford Reforms (1920), the Justice Party won a majority in Madras, but its president declined office. He was:
q.x: P. Theagaraya Chetty declined office and A. Subbarayalu Reddiar became the first Chief Minister; the party won 63 of 98 seats in 1920 and lost power to the Congress in 1937.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a leader of the Justice Party?
q.x: Rajaji was a Congress leader who defeated the Justice Party in 1937; T.M. Nair and Theagaraya Chetty founded the party and the Raja of Panagal was its Chief Minister.

q.s: Desiraju Peda Bapayya of Bapatla, who ran the paper 'Voice of Truth', is remembered as the first practising (Anushthana) follower of the:
q.x: Peda Bapayya was the first Anushthana Brahmo in Andhra; the Pithapuram Raja later endowed the Brahma Dharma Prachara Nidhi.

q.s: The Madras Native Association was founded in 1852 by:
q.x: Gazula Lakshminarasu Chetty, who also ran The Crescent (1844), founded it; its agitation helped bring about the Torture Commission of 1854.

q.s: 'Moturpha', against which the Madras Native Association petitioned, was a tax on:
q.x: Moturpha was a tax on professions, trades and houses in the Madras Presidency.

q.s: The 'Safety Valve' theory about the origin of the Indian National Congress is associated with:
q.x: The theory holds that Hume founded the Congress as a safety valve to channel discontent; Dalhousie is linked with the Doctrine of Lapse and Gandhi with Trusteeship.

q.s: Which of the following ideas is NOT associated with Mahatma Gandhi?
q.x: Hindutva was propounded by V.D. Savarkar; trusteeship, sarvodaya and satyagraha are Gandhian ideas.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of the Extremist leaders of the national movement?
o: Swaraj as gradual self-government within the Empire
Reliance on self-sacrifice and strong will
q.x: Gradual self-government within the Empire was the Moderate goal; for the Extremists Swaraj meant complete self-rule.

q.s: The Hindustan Republican Association (1924), whose members carried out the Kakori train action (1925), was reorganised in 1928 as the:
q.x: The HRA was renamed the HSRA at Delhi in 1928 under Bhagat Singh and Chandrashekhar Azad; the Naujawan Bharat Sabha was formed in 1926.

q.s: The Eka Movement of the early 1920s in the United Provinces was led in its later phase by:
q.x: Madari Pasi led the Eka Movement, which turned violent and slipped out of Congress control; Patel led the non-violent Bardoli Satyagraha (1928).

q.s: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed in the year:
q.x: The pact was signed in March 1931; the Dandi March was in 1930 and the Communal Award and Poona Pact in 1932.

q.s: The Poona Pact (1932) between Gandhi and Ambedkar was a sequel to the:
q.x: Gandhi's fast at Yerawada against separate electorates for the Depressed Classes under the Communal Award led to the Poona Pact in September 1932.

q.s: The death toll in the Jallianwala Bagh firing given by the Congress Punjab Inquiry Committee was about:
q.x: The Congress committee (Motilal Nehru, C.R. Das, Abbas Tyabji, M.R. Jayakar, Gandhi) rejected the official figure of 379 and put the dead at about 1,200.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a member of the Congress Punjab Inquiry Committee on the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
q.x: The committee included Motilal Nehru, C.R. Das, Abbas Tyabji, M.R. Jayakar and Gandhi; Patel was not a member.

q.s: During the Non-Cooperation period, the Moplah uprising of 1921 took place in:
q.x: The Moplah uprising (Aug 1921) was in Malabar; the Akali movement was in Punjab and the Eka movement in the United Provinces.

q.s: The Karachi session of the Congress (1931), which passed the resolution on Fundamental Rights and Economic Policy, was presided over by:
q.x: Patel presided at Karachi; the resolution provided for adult franchise, religious neutrality of the State, free primary education and State ownership of key industries.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a provision of the Karachi resolution on Fundamental Rights and Economic Policy (1931)?
q.x: The resolution provided for adult franchise, free primary education, religious neutrality and State ownership of key industries; it did not provide separate electorates.

q.s: Who moved the Quit India Resolution at the AICC session at Gowalia Tank, Bombay, on 8 August 1942?
q.x: Nehru moved and Patel seconded the resolution; Maulana Azad was then Congress President and the CWC had accepted it at Wardha.

q.s: At the Tripuri session (1939), Subhas Chandra Bose was re-elected Congress President defeating:
q.x: Gandhi said 'Pattabhi's defeat is my defeat'; after the Pant Resolution Bose resigned and Rajendra Prasad became President.

q.s: The Chirala-Perala movement against the municipality tax (1921) was led by:
q.x: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya, 'Andhra Ratna', led the people of Chirala-Perala to leave the town in protest against the new municipality and its taxes.

q.s: The Andhra Mahila Sabha at Madras was founded by:
q.x: Durgabai Deshmukh founded the Andhra Mahila Sabha (1937); Duvvuri Subbamma was known as 'Desabandhavi'.

q.s: The official 'History of the Indian National Congress' (1935) was written by:
q.x: Pattabhi's 1935 history is the official history of the Congress; P. Ananda Charlu presided over the Congress in 1891.

q.s: The first Telugu leader to preside over the Indian National Congress was:
q.x: P. Ananda Charlu presided over the Nagpur session of 1891, long before Pattabhi (Jaipur, 1948).

q.s: Gandhi's autobiography 'The Story of My Experiments with Truth' was originally written in Gujarati and translated into English by:
q.x: Gandhi wrote it in Gujarati; Mahadev Desai translated it into English. Harijan Bandhu was the Gujarati and Harijan Sevak the Hindi edition of Harijan.

q.s: Which of the following journals was NOT associated with Mahatma Gandhi?
q.x: Kesari was Tilak's Marathi paper; Gandhi edited Young India, Navajivan and Harijan (with Harijan Bandhu in Gujarati and Harijan Sevak in Hindi).

q.s: Telugu was made the official language of Andhra Pradesh under the AP Official Languages Act of:
q.x: The Act of 1966 was passed under Article 345, which lets a State Legislature adopt a language used in the State as its official language.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution allows a State Legislature to adopt a language used in the State as its official language?
q.x: Article 345 deals with the official language of a State; 343 with that of the Union and 351 with the development of Hindi.

q.s: The Sribagh Pact (1937), meant to remove the rift within the Andhra movement, was between the leaders of:
q.x: Internal rifts slowed the Andhra movement; the Sribagh Pact of 1937 addressed Rayalaseema's fears of Circar dominance.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the formation of Andhra State is correct?
o: Vizianagaram was one of its districts.
It was inaugurated at Kurnool by Jawaharlal Nehru.
q.x: Andhra State was formed on 1 October 1953 with Kurnool as capital; Vizianagaram district was created only in 1979.

q.s: Who was the first Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh, who called the post of Deputy Chief Minister a "sixth finger"?
q.x: Sanjiva Reddy appointed no Deputy CM; he returned as CM in 1962 after Sanjivayya and resigned in 1964 after the Kurnool bus-routes verdict.

q.s: The Visalandhra Mahasabha was founded at Vijayawada in 1949 under the presidency of:
q.x: Kaleswara Rao founded and presided over the Visalandhra Mahasabha (Nov 1949); Sri Sri presided over the 1954 session at Hyderabad.

q.s: Under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, the Polavaram project was declared a national project by:
q.x: Section 90 declares Polavaram a national project; Section 94 covers fiscal support and Section 97 extends Article 371D to Telangana.

q.s: Which section of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 extended Article 371D to Telangana?
q.x: Section 97 amended Article 371D to extend it to Telangana; Section 94 deals with tax incentives, backward-area packages and support for the new capital.

q.s: The Apex Council for the Krishna and Godavari waters set up under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 is chaired by the:
q.x: The Apex Council is headed by the Union Water Resources (Jal Shakti) Minister with the Chief Ministers of both States as members.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a provision of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
o: An Apex Council for the Krishna and Godavari waters
Hyderabad as the common capital for up to ten years
Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh
q.x: Special Category Status was only the Prime Minister's assurance in the Rajya Sabha; the other three are provisions of the Act.

q.s: The Neolithic site of Palavoy, known for four ash mounds, is in which district?
q.x: Palavoy in Anantapur district is a Neolithic settlement with ash mounds; Patapadu (Kurnool) is known for Chalcolithic painted pottery.

q.s: The Palaeolithic site of Renigunta in Chittoor district is known for its:
q.x: Renigunta yielded an Upper Palaeolithic blade-and-burin industry; Guntakal is known for bone implements.

q.s: Ashoka's reference to the Andhras among the peoples within his empire following Dhamma is found in:
q.x: Rock Edict XIII lists the Andhras among the peoples within the empire; the Aitareya Brahmana gives the first mention of the Andhras.

q.s: The short Sanskrit grammar 'Katantra', said to have been written for the Satavahana king Kuntala Satakarni, is the work of:
q.x: Sarvavarma wrote the Katantra; Gunadhya wrote the Brihatkatha and Kutuhala the Prakrit Lilavati Parinayam.

q.s: The Prakrit work 'Lilavati Parinayam', which tells of Hala's marriage at Draksharama, was written by:
q.x: Kutuhala's Lilavati Parinayam describes Hala's marriage to Lilavati at Draksharama.

q.s: Which of the following statements about women in the Satavahana period is correct?
o: Kings used matronymics such as Gautamiputra.
Women were barred from titles such as Maharathini.
Vetti by women is recorded in the Arthashastra.
Women could not make religious gifts in their own names.
q.x: Matronymics show women's social standing; women made independent gifts, bore titles like Maharathini and Mahabhoji, and the Kamasutra mentions vetti by women.

q.s: The Nasik prasasti describing the achievements of Gautamiputra Satakarni was issued by his mother:
q.x: Gautami Balasri funded the cave-vihara at Nasik and issued the inscription praising her son; Naganika issued the Naneghat inscription.

q.s: The Ikshvaku princess Chamtisri (Santisri), aunt of Virapurushadatta, is known for rebuilding the:
q.x: Chamtisri, the first woman donor at Nagarjunakonda, rebuilt the Maha Chaitya in Virapurushadatta's 6th regnal year and gave nine ayaka pillars.

q.s: Which Vishnukundin ruler is credited with performing 11 Ashvamedhas and a thousand Agnishtomas?
q.x: Madhava Varma II, the greatest Vishnukundin ruler, performed 11 Ashvamedhas; Dantamukha Swami (Ganapati) was installed at Velpuru in his 33rd year.

q.s: The family deity of the Vishnukundins, Sriparvataswami, is identified with:
q.x: Sriparvataswami is the deity of Srisailam (Sriparvata), Mallikarjuna.

q.s: 'Kavirajamarga', the earliest available work on poetics in Kannada, is attributed to the Rashtrakuta king:
q.x: Amoghavarsha I is credited with Kavirajamarga (Kannada) and Prashnottara Ratnamalika (Sanskrit); Trivikrama Bhatta wrote Nalachampu.

q.s: Narayana Bhattu, who helped Nannaya in translating the Mahabharata, bore the title:
q.x: Narayana Bhattu knew eight languages and was called Ashtabhasha Kavisekhara; he received the Nandampudi agrahara, whose grant Nannaya composed.

q.s: Rudradeva, who declared Kakatiya independence and built the Thousand Pillar Temple at Hanamkonda, ascended the throne in:
q.x: Rudradeva (Prataparudra I) came to the throne in 1158; Ganapatideva followed in 1199 and Rudramadevi in 1262.

q.s: The Nayankara system of military fiefs is associated with which dynasty of Andhra?
q.x: Under the Kakatiya Nayankara system Nayakas held villages (Nayakasthalam) instead of salary, kept troops for the king and paid a fixed annual sum.

q.s: Srinatha's 'Sringara Naishadham' is a Telugu rendering of:
q.x: Sringara Naishadham is based on Sriharsha's Naishadhiyacharita; Srinatha is said to have opened the prabandha age in Telugu.

q.s: Rajamahendravaram, the seat of the Reddi kingdom, was annexed after 1446 by:
q.x: Kapilendra Gajapati annexed Rajamahendravaram after 1446, ending the Rajahmundry Reddis.

q.s: The Chagi chiefs of medieval Andhra had their seat at:
q.x: The Chagis ruled from Gudimetta; the Bana kings ruled from Parivipuram (Hindupur) and the Kona Haihayas from Rakuduru.

q.s: The 'Group of Monuments at Hampi' was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in:
q.x: Hampi was inscribed in 1986; its Vittala temple stone chariot appears on the reverse of the Rs 50 note.

q.s: Under Company rule in the Northern Circars, the share of revenue paid by the zamindars to the British was called:
q.x: Peshkash was the zamindar's tribute to the British; korunu was what they collected from farmers, sayer meant transit duties and haveli lands were under direct control.

q.s: Who was the first Chief Minister of Andhra State, whose ministry fell in November 1954?
q.x: Prakasam's ministry fell on 15 November 1954; in the 1955 mid-term elections the Congress won and the CPI was reduced to 15 of 196 seats.

q.s: The Kalukova Satyagraha of 1938 in the Munagala estate was led by:
q.x: Nanduri Prasada Rao led the 1938 Kalukova Satyagraha over the paddy wage; Nayani Venkata Ranga Rao was the zamindar of Munagala.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Bakhtiyar Khalji is correct?
o: His Tibet expedition of 1205 was a success.
He was the real founder of Turk rule in Bihar and Bengal.
He drove Ballala Sena out of Nadiya.
He was a slave of Iltutmish.
q.x: Bakhtiyar Khalji drove Lakshmana Sena out of Nadiya (1204); his Tibet expedition was a disaster. He was an officer under Muhammad Ghori and Aibak.

q.s: In sociology, the primary agent of socialisation is the:
q.x: The family is the first and primary agent of socialisation; by teaching values and norms it promotes social stability.

q.s: An exogamous descent group among Hindus that traces its origin to an ancient rishi is called a:
q.x: A gotra traces descent to a rishi; sapinda kin fall within the prohibited degrees for marriage, and a clan claims descent from a mythical ancestor.

q.s: A descent group whose members can trace actual genealogical links to a common ancestor is known as a:
q.x: A lineage's links are demonstrable; a clan only claims descent from a remote or mythical ancestor.

q.s: 'Caste and Race in India' (1932), which listed six features of caste, was written by:
q.x: Ghurye listed features such as segmental division, hierarchy and lack of free choice of occupation.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of G.S. Ghurye's features of caste?
o: Restrictions on feeding and social intercourse
q.x: Ghurye listed lack of free choice of occupation as a feature, along with segmental division, hierarchy, restrictions on feeding, civil and religious disabilities and endogamy.

q.s: As per Census 2011, the share of urban population in India was about:
q.x: India's urban share was 31.16% (rural 68.8%); Andhra Pradesh's urban share was 29.47% and nearly 90% of STs lived in rural areas.

q.s: The concept of the 'folk-urban continuum' was developed by:
q.x: Redfield developed the folk-urban continuum from his study of Yucatan, Mexico; McKim Marriott gave universalisation and parochialisation.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of a village community?
o: Informal control through caste and custom
Formal social control through law and police
q.x: Village social control is informal; formal control through law and police marks the town or city.

q.s: The Assam Accord of 1985 fixed which date as the cut-off for detecting and deporting foreigners?
q.x: The Assam Accord (15 August 1985) fixed 24 March 1971 as the cut-off date.

q.s: The Mizo Accord, which ended the insurgency and led to Mizoram's statehood in 1987, was signed in:
q.x: The Mizo Accord of 1986 ended the MNF insurgency and Mizoram became a State in 1987.

q.s: Nagaland was made a separate State in the year:
q.x: Nagaland became a State in 1963; 1966 saw the Punjab-Haryana reorganisation with Chandigarh as a Union Territory.

q.s: After the 2008 delimitation, how many Lok Sabha seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes?
q.x: 84 Lok Sabha seats are reserved for SCs and 47 for STs; in Andhra Pradesh, Araku is the ST seat.

q.s: Which of the following Lok Sabha constituencies of Andhra Pradesh is NOT reserved for Scheduled Castes?
q.x: Araku is reserved for STs; Bapatla, Chittoor, Amalapuram and Tirupati are AP's four SC seats.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT regarded as a positive aspect of regionalism?
q.x: Balanced development, cultural pride and local innovation are positive aspects; law-and-order breakdowns and openings for extremists are negative consequences.

q.s: As per Census 2011, youth (15-24 years) formed about what share of India's population?
q.x: Youth aged 15-24 numbered about 231 million (19.1%); adolescents (10-19) numbered about 253 million.

q.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the school mid-day meal scheme is named after:
q.x: The mid-day meal is the Dokka Seethamma scheme; Balamrutham is take-home ration for children 6 months-3 years.

q.s: Which of the following persons is NOT eligible to enrol in the PM Shram Yogi Maan-dhan pension scheme?
o: A member of the National Pension System
q.x: PM-SYM is for unorganised workers aged 18-40; members of EPFO, ESIC or NPS and income-tax payers are excluded.

q.s: The SEED scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment is meant for the economic empowerment of:
q.x: SEED covers DNTs and provides coaching, PM-JAY health cover, PMAY housing and livelihood support.

q.s: Under the Antyodaya Anna Yojana, eligible families receive foodgrains of:
q.x: AAY gives 35 kg per household a month; priority households get 5 kg per person. The NFSA maternity benefit is at least Rs 6,000.

q.s: The minimum maternity benefit for pregnant women under the National Food Security Act, 2013 is:
q.x: Section 4 of the NFSA provides a maternity benefit of not less than Rs 6,000.

q.s: FutureSkills Prime, the digital re-skilling programme for IT professionals, is a joint initiative of MeitY and:
q.x: FutureSkills Prime is a MeitY-NASSCOM initiative with NASSCOM as the implementing partner; C-DAC and NIELIT are resource centres.

q.s: The nodal ministry for the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) is the Ministry of:
q.x: PMKVY (2015), flagship of the Skill India Mission, is run by MSDE; the SANKALP programme is supported by the World Bank.

q.s: The Rules under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 were framed in the year:
q.x: The PoA Rules came in 1995; the Act did not apply to Jammu and Kashmir until 2019.

q.s: The T.M.A. Pai Foundation case (2002) on the rights of minority educational institutions was decided by a Bench of:
q.x: T.M.A. Pai was decided by 11 judges and P.A. Inamdar (2005) by 7 judges.

q.s: Which of the following communities was NOT among the five notified as minorities in 1993?
q.x: Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists and Parsis were notified in 1993; Jains were added as the sixth minority in January 2014.

q.s: As per Census 2011, the second-largest religious minority in India is:
q.x: Christians (2.3%) come after Muslims; Sikhs (1.7%) are third.

q.s: India and Japan describe their relationship as a:
q.x: India-Japan ties were raised to a Special Strategic and Global Partnership in 2014; 'Special and Privileged' describes India-Russia.

q.s: The 16th BRICS Summit, in October 2024, was held at:
q.x: The 16th Summit was at Kazan, Russia; Johannesburg hosted the 15th (2023) and Rio de Janeiro the 17th (2025).

q.s: Which of the following countries was NOT a member of the original BRIC grouping?
q.x: The original BRIC of 2009 was Brazil, Russia, India and China; South Africa joined in 2010-11 to make it BRICS.

q.s: Which of the following reports is NOT published by the IMF?
q.x: Global Economic Prospects is a World Bank report; the WEO, Fiscal Monitor and GFSR are IMF publications.

q.s: The International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC) was agreed in 2000 by India, Iran and:
q.x: INSTC was agreed in 2000 by India, Iran and Russia; India joined the Ashgabat Agreement in 2018.

q.s: The Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project links Kolkata to Mizoram through:
q.x: Kaladan runs Kolkata - Sittwe - Paletwa - Mizoram.

q.s: The port of Duqm, to which India has access for its navy, is located in:
q.x: Duqm is in Oman, Sabang in Indonesia and Agalega in Mauritius.

q.s: Agalega island, where India has helped build an airstrip and jetty, belongs to:
q.x: Agalega is part of Mauritius.

q.s: 'Greyhounds' is the special force of Andhra Pradesh to combat:
q.x: The Greyhounds, AP's anti-LWE force, cut Naxal activity in ASR and Parvathipuram Manyam districts and on the Andhra-Odisha Border.

q.s: The President's power to dissolve the Lok Sabha is provided under:
q.x: Article 85(2) empowers the President to prorogue the Houses and dissolve the Lok Sabha; Articles 86 and 87 cover the address and messages to Parliament.

q.s: Under which Article can the Governor reserve a State Bill for the consideration of the President?
q.x: The Governor's assent and reservation are under Article 200, and the President's action on reserved Bills under Article 201; Article 174 covers summoning and prorogation.

q.s: In I.R. Coelho (2007), the Supreme Court held that laws placed in the Ninth Schedule after which date are open to judicial review?
q.x: 24 April 1973 is the date of the Kesavananda Bharati judgment; later Ninth Schedule entries can be tested against the basic structure.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms is correct?
o: Montagu's declaration on responsible government was made on 20 August 1917.
Dyarchy was introduced at the Centre.
The reforms introduced separate electorates for Muslims for the first time.
Lord Chelmsford was the Secretary of State for India.
q.x: Montagu, the Secretary of State, made the August Declaration; the 1919 Act introduced dyarchy in the provinces, and Muslim separate electorates dated from 1909.

q.s: Separate electorates for Muslims were first introduced by the:
q.x: The Morley-Minto Reforms (1909) introduced separate electorates for Muslims; the 1892 Act introduced indirect election.

q.s: The members of the Constituent Assembly from the provinces were chosen in 1946 by:
q.x: Under the Cabinet Mission Plan the provincial assemblies, elected on the restricted franchise of the 1935 Act, elected the members; princely States' members were nominated.

q.s: The Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act was enacted in the year:
q.x: The Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act came in 1976; the Child Labour Act of 1986 was amended in 2016 to cover adolescents aged 14-18.

q.s: The 2016 amendment to the Child Labour Act prohibits adolescents of which age group from hazardous occupations?
q.x: The amended Act bans all work for children below 14 and hazardous work for adolescents aged 14-18.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Article 14 is correct?
o: 'Equal protection of the laws' is a negative concept.
'Equality before law' is a concept of British origin.
q.x: Equality before law is British and negative; equal protection is American and positive. Article 14 permits reasonable classification but forbids class legislation.

q.s: The concept of 'creamy layer' in reservations originated in the Supreme Court judgment in:
o: State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan (1951)
q.x: Indra Sawhney excluded the creamy layer from OBC reservation; M. Nagaraj (2006) dealt with reservation in promotions.

q.s: The Fundamental Duty of parents to provide opportunities for education to children aged 6-14 (Article 51A(k)) was added by the:
q.x: The 86th Amendment (2002) inserted Article 21A, substituted Article 45 and added 51A(k); the 42nd Amendment had inserted Part IVA with ten duties.

q.s: Privy purses of the former rulers of princely States were abolished by the:
q.x: The 26th Amendment (1971) abolished privy purses; the 25th substituted 'amount' for 'compensation' and inserted Article 31C.

q.s: The Constitutional amendment which abolished the Part A, B, C and D classification of States was the:
q.x: The 7th Amendment (1956) gave effect to the States Reorganisation; the 15th raised the retirement age of High Court judges to 62.

q.s: A joint sitting of the two Houses of Parliament under Article 108 is presided over by the:
o: Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
q.x: The Speaker presides; joint sittings may be held when one House rejects a Bill, the Houses disagree on amendments, or six months pass without passage.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a ground for a joint sitting of the two Houses under Article 108?
o: Rejection of a Bill by the other House
More than six months passing without the Bill being passed
Failure to return a Money Bill within 14 days
q.x: There is no joint sitting on Money Bills; the 14-day limit applies to the Rajya Sabha's handling of a Money Bill.

q.s: The parliamentary device by which all remaining clauses or demands are put to vote when the allotted time is over is called:
q.x: Under the guillotine the remaining items are put to vote, discussed or not; the kangaroo closure takes up only important clauses.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a form of closure motion in Parliament?
q.x: Simple closure, closure by compartments, kangaroo closure and guillotine are closures; adjournment sine die ends a sitting indefinitely.

q.s: How many clear days' notice is ordinarily required for asking a question in Parliament?
q.x: An ordinary question needs 15 clear days' notice; for Zero Hour a member intimates the Presiding Officer on the same day.

q.s: The 'calling attention' device, an Indian innovation in parliamentary procedure, was introduced in:
q.x: Calling attention was introduced in 1954; Zero Hour began in 1962. Calling attention narrowed the use of the adjournment motion.

q.s: Which of the following laws is often cited as an example of a law passed as a Money Bill, bypassing the Rajya Sabha?
q.x: The Aadhaar Act was certified as a Money Bill under Article 110, so it passed without the Rajya Sabha's consent.

q.s: President Giani Zail Singh exercised the pocket veto in 1986 on the:
o: Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Bill
q.x: Zail Singh neither assented to, rejected nor returned the Post Office Bill, simply keeping it pending.

q.s: Which of the following types of veto is NOT available to the President of India?
q.x: The President has absolute, suspensive and pocket vetoes; the qualified veto, which a legislature can override by a higher majority, is not available.

q.s: Under which Article is the State Election Commissioner appointed by the Governor?
q.x: Article 243K provides for the SEC for panchayats (243ZA extends it to municipalities); Article 233 covers district judges.

q.s: Special leave to appeal under Article 136 can be granted by the Supreme Court against any court or tribunal EXCEPT those constituted under:
o: Law relating to the armed forces
q.x: Article 136(2) excludes courts and tribunals under armed forces law; only Parliament, by law, can enlarge the Supreme Court's criminal appellate jurisdiction.

q.s: A High Court judge takes the oath of office before the:
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
q.x: High Court judges are sworn in by the Governor (or a person appointed by him); Supreme Court judges by the President.

q.s: Which of the following statements about judges is correct?
o: A High Court judge takes his oath before the President.
A retired Supreme Court judge may plead in a High Court.
The pension of a High Court judge is charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State.
The salary of a High Court judge is charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State.
q.x: HC judges' salaries are charged on the State's Consolidated Fund but their pensions on the Consolidated Fund of India; a retired SC judge cannot plead in any court.

q.s: Tribunals under Articles 323A and 323B are dealt with in which Part of the Constitution?
q.x: Part XIV-A (added by the 42nd Amendment) covers tribunals; Part IX-B covers co-operative societies and Part VIII Union Territories.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a merit of a unitary form of government?
q.x: Unitary systems give quick decisions, uniform laws and a strong centre; protecting regional identities is a merit of federalism.

q.s: In the Seventh Schedule, 'public order' and 'police' are subjects in the:
q.x: Public order and police are State List entries 1 and 2, which is why States object to Central forces being deployed without their consent.

q.s: Discretionary grants by the Union or a State for any public purpose are made under:
q.x: Article 282 allows grants for any public purpose; Article 275 provides statutory grants-in-aid, including for ST welfare and Scheduled Areas.

q.s: The 'full faith and credit' clause for public acts, records and judicial proceedings is contained in:
q.x: Article 261 gives full faith and credit; 262 deals with inter-State water disputes, 263 with the Inter-State Council and 307 with an authority for inter-State trade.

q.s: The first Indian to qualify for the Indian Civil Service (1864) was:
q.x: Satyendranath Tagore cleared the ICS in 1863-64; the Public Service Commission set up in 1926 had Sir Ross Barker as its first Chairman.

q.s: The first Public Service Commission in India, set up in 1926, was headed by:
q.x: Sir Ross Barker was its first Chairman; the Lee Commission (1923-24) had recommended its setting up.

q.s: Mission Karmayogi for civil service capacity building, launched in 2020, runs on the digital platform:
q.x: Mission Karmayogi runs on iGOT Karmayogi and its custodian is the Capacity Building Commission.

q.s: The power of the Centre to prescribe the tenure and salaries of Information Commissioners was given by the:
q.x: The 2019 amendment removed the fixed five-year term and let the Centre fix tenure and pay by rules.

q.s: Which agency acts as India's National Central Bureau for Interpol?
q.x: The CBI is India's NCB for Interpol and developed the BHARATPOL portal launched in January 2025.

q.s: Which of the following is excluded from the purview of the Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014?
q.x: The SPG is excluded; the 2015 Amendment Bill was passed only by the Lok Sabha and lapsed in 2019.

q.s: In Sarbananda Sonowal v Union of India (2005), the Supreme Court struck down the:
q.x: The IMDT Act was struck down as it violated the Union's duty under Article 355 to protect States against external aggression.

q.s: The Inter-State Council is provided for under:
q.x: The Inter-State Council is under Article 263 (set up in 1990); Zonal Councils were created by the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.

q.s: The Zonal Councils were established under the:
q.x: Zonal Councils are statutory bodies under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956; the NDC was set up by an executive resolution.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an example of cooperative federalism in India?
q.x: State rankings make States compete and show competitive federalism; the GST Council, Inter-State Council and Zonal Councils are forums of cooperation.

q.s: The GST Council is a constitutional body under:
q.x: Article 279A, inserted by the 101st Amendment, provides for the GST Council; the Centre holds one-third and the States two-thirds of the votes.

q.s: Which of the following taxes was NOT subsumed in the GST?
q.x: GST subsumed service tax, VAT, entry tax and other indirect taxes; basic customs duty on imports continues separately.

q.s: The Rajamannar Committee (1969) on Centre-State relations was appointed by the Government of:
q.x: The DMK government of Tamil Nadu appointed it; the Inter-State Council of 1990 came on the Sarkaria Commission's recommendation.

q.s: The Model Code of Conduct was first drafted and used in the Assembly elections of:
q.x: The MCC was first used in the 1960 Kerala election, formalised by the ECI in 1968 and strictly enforced by T.N. Seshan from 1991.

q.s: Reservation of one-third of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies is provided in:
q.x: Article 334A, inserted by the 106th Amendment (2023), reserves seats for women for 15 years after the next census and delimitation.

q.s: Which Constitutional Amendment ended the nomination of Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha?
q.x: The 104th Amendment (2019) extended SC/ST reservation till 2030 but did not extend Anglo-Indian nomination.

q.s: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee, which recommended 'democratic decentralisation', submitted its report in:
q.x: It reported on 24 November 1957 after reviewing the Community Development Programme; the NDC accepted it in January 1958.

q.s: As per Census 2011, which State has the largest Scheduled Tribe population?
q.x: Madhya Pradesh has the largest ST population; STs form about 8.6% of India's population.

q.s: Under Article 334A, seats reserved for women in the Lok Sabha will rotate:
o: Every five years by Presidential order
Every ten years by the Election Commission
q.x: Rotation is after each delimitation; the 15-year period can be extended only by Parliament by law.

q.s: Which of the following statements about a Municipal Corporation is correct?
o: The Municipal Commissioner is appointed by the Mayor.
Its council is headed by the Municipal Commissioner.
It comprises a council, standing committees and a commissioner.
Its area is specified by the President.
q.x: The council is headed by the Mayor, the Commissioner is appointed by the State Government, and the Governor specifies urban areas.

q.s: AMRUT 2.0 was launched in October 2021 by the Ministry of:
q.x: AMRUT 2.0 and the Smart Cities Mission are both run by MoHUA; the Urban Infrastructure Development Fund is operated through the National Housing Bank.

q.s: Which of the following missions is NOT run by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs?
q.x: Jal Jeevan Mission (rural tap water) is under the Ministry of Jal Shakti; AMRUT 2.0, the Smart Cities Mission and PMAY-U are MoHUA missions.

q.s: The sale of a part of a public sector undertaking's equity to the public is known as:
q.x: Disinvestment sells part of PSU equity; privatisation means government leaving ownership or management.

q.s: Which of the following regulators does NOT function under the Ministry of Finance?
q.x: IBBI is under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs; SEBI, IRDAI and PFRDA come under the Ministry of Finance.

q.s: The headquarters of the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) is located at:
q.x: IRDAI is headquartered at Hyderabad; RBI and SEBI at Mumbai.

q.s: Bhogapuram International Airport near Visakhapatnam is being developed under PPP by:
q.x: GMR is developing Bhogapuram; Adani Ports acquired Krishnapatnam (2020) and Gangavaram (2021) ports.

q.s: The State Investment Promotion Board (SIPB) of Andhra Pradesh is chaired by the:
q.x: SIPB is chaired by the Chief Minister; a project with 2,000 or more direct jobs also qualifies as a mega project.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT part of the core infrastructure of the National e-Governance Plan (2006)?
q.x: NeGP's core infrastructure was SWAN, SDCs and CSCs; UMANG came much later (2017).

q.s: The Fund of Funds for Startups under Startup India is managed by:
q.x: The Rs 10,000 crore Fund of Funds is managed by SIDBI; eligible startups get a 3-year tax holiday.

q.s: The Stand-Up India scheme (2016) provides bank loans to:
q.x: Stand-Up India facilitates loans of Rs 10 lakh to Rs 1 crore to SC/ST and women entrepreneurs.

q.s: The ZED certification scheme for MSMEs stands for:
q.x: ZED certifies MSMEs for quality and environment at Bronze, Silver and Gold levels.

q.s: Rashtriya Mahila Kosh provides micro-credit to poor women through:
q.x: RMK, a society under the Societies Registration Act, 1860, lends through NGOs and MFIs.

q.s: DAY-NRLM is implemented by the Ministry of:
q.x: DAY-NRLM (Aajeevika) is a Ministry of Rural Development programme.

q.s: The 'Per Drop More Crop' component of PMKSY deals with:
q.x: Per Drop More Crop promotes drip and sprinkler irrigation; PMKSY was launched on 1 July 2015.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a component of the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana?
q.x: PMKSY combines AIBP, Har Khet Ko Pani, Per Drop More Crop and watershed development; the Soil Health Card is a separate scheme.

q.s: The WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies was adopted at the Ministerial Conference held in 2022, known as:
q.x: Adopted at MC12 (Geneva, 2022), it entered into force in September 2025 and covers marine wild-capture fishing.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh's draft Population Management Policy (2026) marks a shift from:
q.x: Facing falling fertility and ageing, the draft offers incentives for a second or third child and drops the two-child norm for local body polls.

q.s: DAY-NULM is implemented in Andhra Pradesh by:
q.x: The urban mission is implemented by MEPMA and the rural mission by SERP; DAY-NULM comes under MoHUA.

q.s: DAY-NULM replaced which earlier urban scheme in 2013?
q.x: DAY-NULM replaced SJSRY; SGSY was the rural scheme replaced by NRLM.

q.s: The YSR Cheyutha scheme of Andhra Pradesh gives yearly financial aid to SC, ST, BC and minority women of the age group:
q.x: YSR Cheyutha helps women aged 45-60; YSR Aasara repaid SHG loans outstanding on 11 April 2019, and Stree Nidhi gives SHG members credit up to Rs 1 lakh.

q.s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, the gross NPA ratio of scheduled commercial banks fell to a multi-decade low of about:
q.x: Bank GNPA fell to about 2.2%; CPI inflation averaged 1.7% in April-December FY26 and the repo rate was cut by 125 bps since February 2025.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT among the States/UTs that have crossed the upper-middle-income per capita threshold of US $4,636?
q.x: Karnataka, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat and Delhi have crossed US $4,636, while India's per capita income is about US $2,760; Kerala is not in that list.

q.s: India's share in global manufacturing value added is about:
q.x: India holds about 2.9% of global manufacturing value added and about 1.8% of world merchandise exports, and ranks only 44th on the Economic Complexity Index.

q.s: In 1951, agriculture's share of India's workforce was about:
q.x: About 72% of workers were in agriculture in 1951, falling to 64.75% in 1993-94; its share of rural employment has since fallen to about 57%.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Human Development Index is correct?
o: India's HDI of 0.685 (HDR 2025) is in the 'High' category.
It is published by the World Bank.
Since 2010 it is the arithmetic mean of the three dimension indices.
Income is measured in PPP dollars.
q.x: UNDP's HDI uses PPP dollars and, since 2010, the geometric mean; India's 0.685 is in the 'Medium' category.

q.s: The Third United Nations Decade for the Eradication of Poverty covers the period:
q.x: The UN General Assembly proclaimed the Third Decade for 2018-2027; SDG 1 aims to end poverty, while ending hunger is SDG 2.

q.s: The concept of the 'Rolling Plan', followed in India during 1978-80, was suggested by:
q.x: Gunnar Myrdal suggested the rolling plan; the Janata government used it from April 1978 to March 1980.

q.s: The main feature of the Rolling Plan was that:
o: Plans were made at the village level alone
Targets were fixed for fifteen years
Only the private sector was planned
Allocations and targets were revised every year
q.x: Under the rolling plan, targets were revised annually; this gave flexibility but weakened commitment to targets.

q.s: The Eighth Five Year Plan, delayed by political instability and the balance-of-payments crisis, finally began in:
q.x: The 1990-91 crisis led to Annual Plans for 1990-92, and the Eighth Plan started in April 1992.

q.s: The 'Plan Holiday' of 1966-69, when Annual Plans were adopted, followed the failure of the:
q.x: The Third Plan fell far short of its 5.6% target because of the 1962 and 1965 wars and the 1965-66 droughts, so three Annual Plans followed.

q.s: In June 1991, on the eve of the economic reforms, India's foreign exchange reserves had fallen to about:
q.x: Reserves were about $975 million, barely two weeks of imports; growth in 1991-92 was below 1% and the share of agriculture in GDP fell in later years.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Fifteenth Finance Commission is correct?
o: It was chaired by N.K. Singh.
It gave a single report for 2020-25.
It was chaired by Y.V. Reddy.
q.x: The 15th FC, constituted under Article 280 and chaired by N.K. Singh, gave two reports - for 2020-21 and for 2021-26; Y.V. Reddy chaired the 14th.

q.s: The Atal Innovation Mission was set up in 2016 by:
q.x: NITI Aayog set up AIM in 2016; its 'Strategy for New India @75' came out in 2018.

q.s: The Swadesh Darshan and PRASHAD schemes of the Ministry of Tourism were launched in:
q.x: Both schemes date from 2014-15; India ranked 39th in the Travel & Tourism Development Index 2024.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a scheme of the Ministry of Tourism?
q.x: AMRUT is an urban mission of MoHUA; Swadesh Darshan, PRASHAD and Dekho Apna Desh are tourism schemes.

q.s: Which institution acts as the supervisor of Regional Rural Banks and cooperative banks?
q.x: NABARD supervises RRBs and cooperative banks; SIDBI oversees State Financial Corporations and NHB supervises housing finance companies.

q.s: The State Bank of India was formed on 1 July 1955 by taking over the:
q.x: SBI was formed from the Imperial Bank of India in 1955; the RBI was nationalised on 1 January 1949 and the LIC formed on 1 September 1956.

q.s: The Reserve Bank of India was nationalised on:
q.x: The RBI, set up on 1 April 1935, was nationalised on 1 January 1949; 14 banks were nationalised on 19 July 1969.

q.s: The first bank in India with wholly Indian capital and management (1894) was:
q.x: PNB was founded in 1894 at Lahore; Allahabad Bank (1865) was the oldest joint-stock bank and Oudh Commercial Bank (1881) the first limited-liability bank managed by Indians.

q.s: Which of the following price indices in India measures changes in retail prices?
q.x: CPI tracks retail prices and is used for the RBI's inflation target; WPI tracks wholesale prices.

q.s: Core inflation excludes the prices of:
q.x: Core inflation leaves out the volatile food and fuel items; headline inflation includes them.

q.s: In May 2026, the retail inflation of Andhra Pradesh, which stayed above the national rate for five consecutive months, was:
q.x: AP's retail inflation was 4.9% against India's 3.9% in May 2026.

q.s: Which of the following statements about deficits is correct?
o: Primary deficit is always greater than fiscal deficit.
Effective revenue deficit can exceed revenue deficit.
A zero primary deficit means the government borrows only to pay interest.
q.x: Fiscal deficit = primary deficit + interest; effective revenue deficit is revenue deficit minus grants for capital assets, so it cannot exceed it.

q.s: If a government's fiscal deficit is Rs 1,50,000 crore and its interest payments are Rs 1,20,000 crore, its primary deficit is:
q.x: Primary deficit = 1,50,000 - 1,20,000 = Rs 30,000 crore; the fiscal deficit is the headline marker of fiscal health.

q.s: Asia's first Export Processing Zone was set up in 1965 at:
q.x: Kandla (Gujarat) had Asia's first EPZ; the SEZ policy came in April 2000 and the SEZ Act in 2005.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Special Economic Zones is correct?
o: An SEZ is treated as foreign territory for trade and tariff purposes.
Asia's first EPZ was set up at Santacruz.
The SEZ Act came in 2000 and the policy in 2005.
The SEZ concept was first proposed in the EXIM Policy 1992-97.
q.x: The SEZ policy came in 2000 (from the EXIM Policy 1997-2002) and the Act in 2005; Asia's first EPZ was at Kandla (1965).

q.s: The RoDTEP scheme for exporters replaced the:
q.x: RoDTEP replaced the MEIS, which was ruled against at the WTO; it refunds embedded taxes and is run online by the CBIC.

q.s: The primary aim of RBI intervention in the foreign exchange market is to:
o: Curb excessive volatility of the rupee
q.x: India has a managed float; the RBI intervenes to curb volatility, not to defend any fixed level.

q.s: In an RBI forex buy/sell swap of the kind used to support the rupee:
o: Banks lend dollars to exporters at zero interest
The RBI prints rupees to buy gold
Banks sell dollars to the RBI and buy them back later at a premium
The RBI sells government bonds abroad
q.x: In such a swap, banks sell dollars to the RBI and repurchase them later; spot intervention means selling dollars from the reserves.

q.s: Under the RBI framework of November 2024, FPI holdings above what share of a listed company's equity can be reclassified as FDI?
q.x: Holdings of 10% or more are FDI; under the General Route FPIs may hold up to 6% of Central and 2% of State Government securities.

q.s: Which of the following statements about land use is correct?
o: Forests are 50% of Andhra Pradesh's land-use classification.
Andhra Pradesh's cropping intensity rose from 1.21 to 1.25 between 2016-17 and 2023-24.
Forest cover is 21.71% of India's geographical area as per ISFR 2021.
India's net sown area is more than half its geographical area.
q.x: Net sown area is about 42.8% of India's area; AP's cropping intensity fell from 1.25 to 1.21, and forests are about 22.63% of AP's land use.

q.s: India's record wheat production of 113.29 million tonnes was achieved in the year:
q.x: Wheat output reached 113.29 MT in 2023-24; India is both the largest producer and the largest consumer of pulses.

q.s: Under PM-AASHA, the component that pays farmers the difference between MSP and the market price without physical procurement is:
q.x: The Price Deficiency Payment Scheme pays MSP minus market price; PSS involves physical procurement by NAFED and NCCF.

q.s: The Market Intervention Scheme (MIS) applies to:
o: Perishable commodities not covered by MSP
q.x: MIS covers perishables like fruits and vegetables outside MSP, triggered by a fall in price of at least 10%.

q.s: From 1 April 2025, a micro enterprise is one with investment up to Rs 2.5 crore and turnover up to:
q.x: The revised limits: micro Rs 2.5 crore/Rs 10 crore, small Rs 25 crore/Rs 100 crore, medium Rs 125 crore/Rs 500 crore.

q.s: India reached 50% non-fossil installed power capacity in 2025, how many years ahead of its 2030 NDC target?
q.x: The 50% non-fossil capacity NDC target for 2030 was met in 2025; India ranked 23rd in CCPI 2026.

q.s: Which country topped the World Happiness Report 2018?
q.x: Finland topped WHR 2018 and has done so since; Switzerland led in 2015, Denmark in 2016 and Norway in 2017.

q.s: The Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction (BIFR) was set up under the:
q.x: BIFR under SICA failed because a reference froze creditors' recovery and suffered procedural delays; it was replaced by the IBC regime.

q.s: The largest port of Andhra Pradesh by cargo handled is:
q.x: Visakhapatnam is AP's biggest port; in 2024-25 AP was the sixth largest exporting State.

q.s: Under Section 5 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, Hyderabad was the common capital of the two States till:
q.x: Hyderabad was the common capital for up to 10 years from 2 June 2014; the 2026 amendment inserted Section 5(3) making Amaravati the sole capital.

q.s: Schedule X of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, which lists 142 institutions, deals with:
q.x: Schedule X lists 142 State institutions; Schedule IX lists 91 government companies and corporations.

q.s: In Andhra Pradesh's 2026-27 budget, interest payments form about what share of revenue receipts?
q.x: Interest of Rs 37,281 crore is about 16% of revenue receipts, while pensions are about 10%.

q.s: Under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, refunds of taxes other than property tax collected in excess are divided between the two States:
q.x: Section 56 divides refunds by population while Section 50 divides arrears by place of assessment; the mismatch cost AP about Rs 3,900 crore.

q.s: Schedule IX of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 covers:
q.x: Schedule IX lists 91 companies and corporations (including APSFC); Schedule X lists 142 institutions.

q.s: Under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, most assets were divided by location, while liabilities were divided mainly by:
q.x: Since major assets lay in Hyderabad, the location rule favoured Telangana, while debt went by population (AP about 58%), so AP got about 46% of revenue but about 58% of debt.

q.s: Zero Budget Natural Farming (ZBNF) was developed in the mid-1990s by:
q.x: Subhash Palekar developed ZBNF; 'zero budget' means no purchased inputs. AP launched it in 2016, and it is now called APCNF.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh's natural farming programme, earlier called ZBNF, is now known as:
q.x: It was renamed AP Community-managed Natural Farming (APCNF); PKVY is a separate Central scheme.

q.s: The main reason for the conversion of paddy land to aquaculture in the Godavari delta is:
o: Higher returns from shrimp and fish farming
q.x: Shrimp and fish farming give much higher returns than paddy, so delta farmers have converted their fields to ponds.

q.s: In Andhra Pradesh, Rythu Bazars are mainly used as a quick market-intervention channel for:
q.x: The Government procures perishables through Rythu Bazars to stabilise prices; they are not used for foodgrains.

q.s: The Andhra Pradesh Industrial Infrastructure Corporation (APIIC) was set up in:
q.x: APIIC was set up on 26 September 1973; it holds a land bank of about 41,998 acres and can allot up to 50 acres without Cabinet approval.

q.s: MAARG, launched under Startup India, is a national platform for:
q.x: MAARG is a mentorship platform for start-ups of all sectors; the National Startup Advisory Council was notified in January 2020.

q.s: The Budget 2026-27 raised the Securities Transaction Tax on futures and options mainly to:
o: Lower the fiscal deficit by half
q.x: STT on futures went from 0.02% to 0.05% and on options from 0.10% to 0.15% to curb speculation.

q.s: The change of seasons on the Earth is caused by:
o: The varying distance of the Moon
Revolution of the Earth with its axis tilted
q.x: Seasons result from revolution with the 23½° tilt; rotation causes day and night and the equatorial bulge.

q.s: Spring tides occur when:
o: The Sun and Moon are at right angles to the Earth
The Sun, Earth and Moon are in a straight line
q.x: At new and full moon, the Sun, Earth and Moon line up and their pulls combine to give spring tides; neap tides come when they are at right angles.

q.s: The Koyna earthquake of 1967 is a well-known example of a:
q.x: Koyna (Maharashtra) is attributed to reservoir loading; Latur (Killari, 1993) was an intraplate earthquake in the stable shield.

q.s: Which of the following statements about intrusive igneous landforms is correct?
o: A batholith is the largest, deep-seated intrusive mass.
A dyke is a horizontal sheet lying along the layers.
A sill is a near-vertical wall cutting across rock layers.
A laccolith is a saucer-shaped body sagging downward.
q.x: A batholith is exposed only after erosion; a sill is horizontal, a dyke vertical, a laccolith dome-shaped and a lopolith saucer-shaped.

q.s: Which of the following statements about volcanic eruptions is correct?
o: Lahars come mainly from shield volcanoes.
Carbon dioxide is the most abundant volcanic gas.
Water vapour is the most abundant volcanic gas.
Sulphate aerosols from eruptions warm the Earth for years.
q.x: Water vapour comes first and CO2 second; lahars are mainly from stratovolcanoes, and sulphate aerosols cool the Earth.

q.s: Lahars, or volcanic mudflows, are mainly associated with:
q.x: Lahars come mainly from steep stratovolcanoes, often snow-capped.

q.s: Rivers like the Indus, Sutlej and Brahmaputra, which are older than the Himalaya and cut deep gorges as the land rose, are examples of:
q.x: An antecedent river keeps its course by downcutting as the land rises, giving gorges.

q.s: Which of the following rivers is NOT an example of antecedent drainage?
q.x: The Indus, Sutlej and Brahmaputra are older than the Himalaya; the Godavari is a peninsular river following the eastward slope of the plateau.

q.s: The Strait of Hormuz connects the Persian Gulf with the:
q.x: The Strait of Hormuz lies between Iran and Oman and joins the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman.

q.s: The largest river island of India, Majuli, lies on the river:
q.x: Majuli in Assam lies on the Brahmaputra.

q.s: Hong Kong was returned by Britain to China in the year:
q.x: Hong Kong was handed back in 1997; Macau was returned by Portugal in 1999.

q.s: When air is heated, it:
o: Expands, becomes less dense and creates low pressure
Contracts, becomes denser and creates high pressure
q.x: Heated air expands and its density falls, giving low pressure; cooled air contracts and gives high pressure.

q.s: A front formed when a cold front overtakes a warm front is called:
q.x: An occluded front forms when the faster cold front catches up with the warm front; a stationary front is one where neither air mass advances.

q.s: Prolonged light to moderate rain over a wide area along a gentle slope is typical of a:
q.x: A warm front has a gentle slope and long steady rain; a cold front is steep, with cumulonimbus and heavy short showers.

q.s: Which of the following statements about measuring scales is correct?
o: Category 1 on the Saffir-Simpson scale has winds of 178-208 km/h.
On the Beaufort scale, a gale corresponds to force 8.
The Beaufort scale measures earthquake intensity.
The Richter scale was devised in 1955.
q.x: The Beaufort scale (0-12) measures wind force; Richter devised his scale in 1935, and Category 1 is 119-153 km/h (178-208 km/h is Category 3).

q.s: The El Nino phenomenon is generally associated with:
q.x: El Nino brings warmer central and eastern Pacific waters and tends to weaken the monsoon; La Nina brings stronger trade winds and a good monsoon.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT associated with La Nina?
q.x: La Nina usually brings a good monsoon; a weak monsoon is linked with El Nino.

q.s: In the heterosphere, the gas that dominates the highest layer, being the lightest, is:
q.x: Gases in the heterosphere are layered by molecular weight: nitrogen, atomic oxygen, helium and hydrogen from lower to higher levels.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a cause of ocean currents?
q.x: Winds, temperature and salinity differences (with the Coriolis force) cause currents; the Earth's revolution does not.

q.s: The highest plateau in India is the:
q.x: The Ladakh Plateau in the Trans-Himalaya is India's highest; the Trans-Himalaya is older than the Himalayas.

q.s: Which of the following ranges is NOT a part of the Trans-Himalaya?
q.x: The Karakoram, Ladakh and Zaskar ranges form the Trans-Himalaya; the Pir Panjal is part of the Lesser Himalaya.

q.s: The east coast of India is described as a largely:
q.x: The east coast has risen relative to the sea and has a wide shelf, beaches, bars, lagoons and deltas.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the east coast of India?
o: Lagoons such as Chilika and Pulicat
q.x: The emergent east coast has a wide continental shelf, deltas, lagoons and beaches; a narrow shelf is typical of the west coast.

q.s: As per ISFR 2023, which State has the largest mangrove cover in India?
q.x: West Bengal, with the Sundarbans, has the largest mangrove cover; Gujarat is second.

q.s: In the revised coastline figures, Andhra Pradesh has a coastline of 1,053.07 km and ranks:
q.x: AP ranks third after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu; under the old figure of 974 km it was second. The national total rose to 11,098.81 km because of finer GIS mapping.

q.s: The Tamil Nadu coast receives most of its rainfall during:
o: June-September, from the Arabian Sea branch
q.x: Tamil Nadu lies in the rain shadow of the Western Ghats in June-September; its main rain comes from the north-east monsoon.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a flood-mitigation measure?
q.x: Rock bolting stabilises slopes against landslides; embankments, dams and channel improvement mitigate floods.

q.s: The Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre, opened in 2007, is located at:
q.x: After the 2004 tsunami, India set up its warning centre at INCOIS, Hyderabad.

q.s: The Bhagirathi river rises at:
q.x: The Bhagirathi rises at Gomukh; the Alaknanda rises at the Satopanth glacier, and Badrinath lies on it.

q.s: Which of the following places does NOT lie on the Alaknanda river?
q.x: Kedarnath lies on the Mandakini, which joins the Alaknanda at Rudraprayag; Badrinath and Joshimath are on the Alaknanda.

q.s: The Dasam Falls in Jharkhand is located on the river:
q.x: Dasam Falls is on the Kanchi, Jonha on the Rarhu, and Amritdhara on the Hasdeo in Chhattisgarh.

q.s: The Polavaram project, a National Project under Section 90 of the AP Reorganisation Act, is built across the river:
q.x: Polavaram is an earth-cum-rockfill dam on the Godavari, first planned as Ramapada Sagar by K.L. Rao.

q.s: Alkaline (sodic) soils are commonly reclaimed by applying:
q.x: Gypsum is used for sodic soils and lime for acidic soils; reh, kallar and usar are local names for saline-alkaline soils.

q.s: Saline and alkaline soils are formed mainly because of:
q.x: Over-irrigation with poor drainage brings salts to the surface; Gujarat has the largest saline area.

q.s: The AP Forest Department's wood bank at Tirupati mainly holds:
q.x: Tirupati holds red sanders, Kapavaram teak and Rajamahendravaram bamboo.

q.s: TRIFED functions under the Ministry of:
q.x: TRIFED was set up in 1987 under the Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act and works under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs.

q.s: The Girijan Co-operative Corporation (GCC) of Andhra Pradesh has its headquarters at:
q.x: GCC, which markets minor forest produce, is headquartered at Visakhapatnam.

q.s: Hyderabad falls in which seismic zone of India?
q.x: Hyderabad is in Zone II, the least earthquake-prone; the Amaravati region is in Zone III, Delhi in Zone IV and Guwahati in Zone V.

q.s: Which of the following places is NOT in Seismic Zone V?
q.x: Delhi is in Zone IV; the North-East, Kashmir and Kutch (Bhuj) are in Zone V.

q.s: The Indian Standard that carries the seismic zoning map of India is:
q.x: IS 1893 contains the seismic zone map; IS 13920 deals with ductile detailing. Andhra Pradesh has no area in Zone V.

q.s: Which of the following is a non-structural landslide mitigation measure?
q.x: Hazard zonation, early warning and land-use regulation are non-structural; retaining walls, rock bolting, mesh and drainage are structural.

q.s: In 2026, which two hazards were added to the notified list of disasters eligible for SDRF assistance?
q.x: On the 16th Finance Commission's recommendation the list went from 12 to 14 for 2026-31 by adding heatwaves and lightning.

q.s: The State Disaster Management Authority is headed by the:
q.x: Under the DM Act, 2005 the SDMA is headed by the Chief Minister; the NDMA by the Prime Minister and the DDMA by the Collector, with the elected local head as co-chairperson.

q.s: The leading salt-producing State of India is:
q.x: Gujarat produces the bulk of India's salt; AP's coastline is 1,053.07 km and the Vamsadhara and Nagavali drain northern AP.

q.s: The Pinnapuram integrated renewable energy project with pumped storage, developed by Greenko, is in which district?
q.x: Pinnapuram PSP (1,680 MW) is in Kurnool district; the Kurnool Ultra Mega Solar Park is at Panyam.

q.s: Which of the following statements about grades of coal is correct?
o: Palana lignite field is in Gujarat.
Peat, with less than 40% carbon, is the first stage of coal formation.
Lignite has a low moisture content.
Indian anthracite occurs mainly in Jharkhand.
q.x: Lignite has high moisture; Indian anthracite occurs only in Jammu and Kashmir, and Palana is in Rajasthan.

q.s: The highest grade of coal, with 80-95% carbon, is:
q.x: Anthracite has the most carbon and occurs in India only in Jammu and Kashmir; peat, with under 40% carbon, is the first stage of coal formation.

q.s: The Dalhan Aatmanirbharta Mission (2025) assures 100% MSP procurement for four years of all the following pulses EXCEPT:
q.x: Announced in October 2025, the mission assures full procurement of tur, urad and masoor only.

q.s: The Central Institute of Freshwater Aquaculture (CIFA) is located at:
q.x: CIFA is at Bhubaneswar, CMFRI at Kochi, CSWRI at Avikanagar and the High Security Animal Disease Laboratory at Bhopal.

q.s: The High Security Animal Disease Laboratory of ICAR is located at:
q.x: HSADL at Bhopal handles exotic and emerging animal diseases such as avian influenza.

q.s: The headquarters of Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU) is at:
q.x: ANGRAU is headquartered at Lam, Guntur; Chintaladeevi (Nellore) has a National Kamdhenu Breeding Centre.

q.s: The State Advised Price (SAP) of sugarcane is fixed by the:
q.x: States fix the SAP while the Centre fixes the Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP); the Rangarajan Committee recommended 70:30 revenue sharing.

q.s: India's first Kisan Rail (2020) ran between:
q.x: The first Kisan Rail ran Devlali (Nashik) - Danapur on 7 August 2020; India's first hydrogen train runs Jind-Sonipat.

q.s: India's first hydrogen-powered train runs on the route:
q.x: The hydrogen train runs Jind-Sonipat in Haryana; Tejas Express first ran Mumbai-Karmali in 2017.

q.s: The North-South and East-West Corridors of the National Highways meet at:
q.x: The two corridors intersect at Jhansi; NH 44 (Srinagar-Kanyakumari) is the longest National Highway.

q.s: Which is the longest National Highway of India?
q.x: NH 44 runs from Srinagar to Kanyakumari; NH 16 runs along the east coast through Andhra Pradesh.

q.s: The Digital India programme was launched on:
q.x: Digital India began on 1 July 2015; PM-WANI for public Wi-Fi came in December 2020 and NOFN, the precursor of BharatNet, in 2011.

q.s: As per Census 2011, the gender gap in literacy was widest in:
q.x: Rajasthan had the widest gap (about 28 points); ST literacy (59%) was lower than SC literacy (66.1%).

q.s: Among the districts of Andhra Pradesh, the lowest literacy rate is in:
q.x: Alluri Sitarama Raju district has the lowest literacy (44.67%); Visakhapatnam has the highest urbanisation.

q.s: India's child sex ratio in Census 2001 was:
q.x: The child sex ratio fell from 927 (2001) to 919 (2011) while the overall sex ratio rose from 933 to 943.

q.s: India's female labour force participation rate (15+) rose from 23.3% in 2017-18 to about what in 2022-23?
q.x: FLFPR rose to 37% in 2022-23 and about 40% in 2025; on Claudia Goldin's U-curve India was on the falling half till 2018-19.

q.s: The Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PCPNDT) Act was enacted in:
q.x: The PNDT Act of 1994 was renamed PCPNDT in 2003; it bans sex selection.

q.s: As per Census 2011, the district with the highest sex ratio (1,019) in present Andhra Pradesh was:
q.x: Vizianagaram had the highest sex ratio, Srikakulam came second and Anantapuramu had the lowest (977).

q.s: In the 2009 genetic framework of Indian population history, 'ANI' and 'ASI' stand for:
o: Aryan Northern Immigrants and Austric Southern Indigenes
Ancestral North Indians and Ancestral South Indians
Asian Nomadic Invaders and African Settled Inhabitants
Ancient Neolithic Indians and Ancient Stone-age Indians
q.x: Most Indians descend from a mix of ANI and ASI; Rakhigarhi DNA showed no Steppe Pastoralist gene.

q.s: Which of the following States has NO notified Scheduled Tribe?
q.x: Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Chandigarh and Puducherry have no notified STs; STs numbered 10.43 crore (8.6%) in 2011.
