q.s: The three-language formula was first adopted in the:
q.x: The Kothari Commission's three-language formula was adopted in the NPE 1968; UNESCO lists about 197 endangered Indian languages.

q.s: Which of the following statements about India's Biosphere Reserves in UNESCO's World Network is correct?
o: The Nilgiri was the first to be included, in 2000.
All 18 Indian Biosphere Reserves are in the network.
The Great Rann of Kutch is in the network.
q.x: 13 of India's 18 BRs are in the network; the Nilgiri came first in 2000, and Panna was included in 2020.

q.s: The only elephant habitat of Andhra Pradesh, along with the Rayala Elephant Reserve, is the:
q.x: Elephants moved into Palamaner in the 1980s after drought in Hosur-Dharmapuri and Bannerghatta; Koundinya WLS is their habitat.

q.s: In the demographic transition model, India during 1951-81 was in the:
q.x: Before 1921 India was in stage 1 (high stationary); 1951-81 was stage 2 (early expanding, falling death rate, high birth rate); India is now in stage 3.

q.s: All three UN World Conferences on Disaster Risk Reduction, including the one that adopted the Sendai Framework, were hosted by:
q.x: Yokohama (1994), Kobe (2005) and Sendai (2015) were the venues; UNDRR convenes the Global Platform for DRR.

q.s: The Department of Atomic Energy was set up in 1954 by:
o: A Cabinet resolution of the Planning Commission
q.x: DAE was created by Presidential order in 1954; the Atomic Energy Commission dates from 1948. DAE and the Department of Space are under the PM.

q.s: The nodal department for the National Quantum Mission is the:
q.x: The NQM, approved on 19 April 2023, is run by DST; it targets 50-1000 qubit computers and satellite-based QKD over 2000 km.

q.s: 'Cervavac', developed by the Serum Institute of India, is a vaccine against:
q.x: Cervavac is India's indigenous quadrivalent HPV vaccine; Rotavac of Bharat Biotech targets rotavirus.

q.s: A.M. Chakrabarty is known for developing a genetically engineered bacterium capable of:
q.x: His oil-eating Pseudomonas putida led to Diamond v. Chakrabarty (1980), the first patent on a living organism.

q.s: Which of the following statements about nanotechnology tools is correct?
o: The Atomic Force Microscope can image non-conducting surfaces.
The Scanning Tunnelling Microscope works only on non-conductors.
q.x: The AFM works on non-conductors too while the STM needs conducting surfaces; lithography is top-down and self-assembly bottom-up.

q.s: The term 'Internet of Things' was coined in 1999 by:
q.x: Kevin Ashton coined the term; the three-layer IoT model is perception - network - application.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a layer of the basic three-layer IoT architecture?
q.x: The three-layer model is perception - network - application; the four-stage model adds a transport layer.

q.s: Which of the following statements about lithium-ion batteries is correct?
o: Graphite is generally used as the anode.
During discharge, Li+ ions move from cathode to anode.
They use lead dioxide as the cathode.
q.x: Graphite is the anode and LFP or NMC the cathode; on discharge Li+ ions move from anode to cathode.

q.s: The Pinnapuram project in Kurnool district is notable for combining solar and wind power with:
q.x: Greenko's Pinnapuram integrated project pairs solar and wind with pumped hydro storage.

q.s: Kalamsat-V2, built by students of Space Kidz India, was launched in January 2019 by:
q.x: PSLV-C44 carried Kalamsat-V2, the first payload to use the PS4 stage as an orbital platform.

q.s: The HOPE analogue habitat in Ladakh, chosen for its Mars-like conditions, is located at:
q.x: HOPE was set up at Tso Kar for high UV, low pressure and cold; India's first analogue mission was at Leh in November 2024.

q.s: Nirbhay, developed by DRDO, is a:
q.x: Nirbhay flies at about Mach 0.8; BrahMos is supersonic. Cruise missiles are powered throughout by air-breathing engines.

q.s: 'Nag', developed under the IGMDP, is a:
q.x: Nag is a fire-and-forget anti-tank missile that guides itself after launch; Prithvi is the surface-to-surface and Akash the surface-to-air missile.

q.s: Which of the following missiles was NOT developed under the Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme?
q.x: Prithvi, Agni, Akash, Trishul and Nag were IGMDP missiles; BrahMos is an Indo-Russian joint venture.

q.s: e-Kranti (NeGP 2.0), approved in 2015, contains how many Mission Mode Projects?
q.x: e-Kranti has 44 MMPs and the vision 'Transforming e-Governance for Transforming Governance'; the original NeGP had 27.

q.s: APSCAN, the Andhra Pradesh Secretariat Campus Area Network (2016), is located at:
q.x: APSCAN serves the Velagapudi Secretariat; the State Data Centre is at Mangalagiri.

q.s: A ransomware attack that prevents doctors from accessing hospital records violates which principle of the CIA triad?
q.x: Availability means data remain accessible to authorised users; confidentiality guards against illicit access and integrity against alteration.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a principle of the CIA triad of information security?
q.x: CIA stands for Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability; authentication is a separate security control.

q.s: Under the DPDP Act, 2023, the maximum penalty for failure to take reasonable security safeguards against a personal data breach is:
q.x: Security safeguards failure attracts up to Rs 250 crore, breach of children's data obligations Rs 200 crore and SDF duties Rs 150 crore.

q.s: Which of the following statements about nuclear power in India is correct?
o: India's PHWR unit sizes have grown from 220 MW to 540 MW to 700 MW.
Tarapur has 700 MW PHWRs built by Russia.
q.x: MAPS is at Kalpakkam, Kudankulam runs Russian VVERs, and Tarapur's first units are US-built BWRs.

q.s: MAPS, India's first fully indigenous PHWR station, is located at:
q.x: The Madras Atomic Power Station is at Kalpakkam; Tarapur has India's first nuclear plant with US-built BWRs.

q.s: The Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB) was constituted in 1983 by:
o: An executive order under the Atomic Energy Act, 1962
q.x: AERB was set up by executive order and worked under DAE; it also regulates radiation safety in medical and industrial uses.

q.s: India's first sovereign green bonds were issued in:
q.x: Sovereign green bonds were first issued in January 2023; IREDA got Navratna status in April 2024.

q.s: The Hydrocarbon Exploration and Licensing Policy (HELP) provides for:
o: A single licence for all hydrocarbons
Separate licences for oil and gas
q.x: HELP gives one licence for conventional and unconventional hydrocarbons; ONGC Videsh acquires oil and gas assets abroad.

q.s: Under the National Policy on Biofuels, 100% FDI under the automatic route is allowed in biofuel technology provided the biofuels are for:
q.x: Automatic-route FDI is allowed only where the biofuels are for domestic use; Section 52 of the Motor Vehicles Act permits engine conversion to biofuels.

q.s: In 2014, the largest source of installed renewable power capacity in India was:
q.x: In 2014 wind capacity was about 21 GW against only 2.8 GW of solar; solar has since overtaken wind.

q.s: At 150 m hub height, which State has the highest wind power potential in India?
q.x: Rajasthan leads at 150 m; AP's potential at 120 m (about 74.90 GW) is below Gujarat, Rajasthan and Karnataka.

q.s: According to the biogeographic classification of Rodgers and Panwar, India is divided into how many biogeographic zones?
q.x: India has 10 biogeographic zones and 25 provinces, falling into 5 biomes; the classification is by the Wildlife Institute of India.

q.s: Which of the following statements about India's biogeographic classification is correct?
o: India lies in the Palearctic and Afrotropical realms.
It was drawn up by the Botanical Survey of India.
India's biogeographic zones fall into 5 biomes.
India is divided into 25 biogeographic zones.
q.x: Rodgers and Panwar (Wildlife Institute of India) gave 10 zones and 25 provinces in 5 biomes, within the Palearctic and Indo-Malayan realms.

q.s: In the Red Data Book, green pages are used for species that are:
q.x: Green pages show recovered species; the IUCN Red List, started in 1964, measures extinction risk and the Green Status (2021) measures recovery.

q.s: The 14th Conference of Parties (COP14) of the UNCCD was held in 2019 at:
q.x: COP14 was at New Delhi in 2019; COP17 was held at Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, in 2026.

q.s: Kolleru Lake, a Ramsar site and wildlife sanctuary of Andhra Pradesh, lies between the deltas of:
q.x: Kolleru lies between the Godavari and Krishna deltas and was declared a Ramsar site in 2002.

q.s: The National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) is chaired by the:
q.x: NTCA is a statutory body under the 2006 amendment of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, chaired by the Union Environment Minister; a Tiger Conservation Plan is mandatory for every reserve.

q.s: The Hornbill Nest Adoption Programme is associated with which tiger reserve?
q.x: Pakke (Arunachal Pradesh) runs the Hornbill Nest Adoption Programme; Ratapani became the 57th and Madhav the 58th tiger reserve.

q.s: Swachh Survekshan, the annual cleanliness survey of cities, is conducted by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs through the:
q.x: The QCI conducts the survey (since 2016); Swachh Survekshan Grameen is run by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. Indore and Surat shared the top spot in 2023.

q.s: The Directive Principle directing the State to protect and improve the environment and safeguard forests and wildlife is:
q.x: Article 48A (42nd Amendment) is a duty of the State; Article 51A(g) is the corresponding fundamental duty of citizens.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Central Pollution Control Board is correct?
o: It was constituted in 1974 under the Air Act.
It coordinates the activities of the State Pollution Control Boards.
Its chairperson is nominated by the State Governments.
It was constituted under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
q.x: The CPCB was set up in 1974 under the Water Act and coordinates the SPCBs; the Air Act came in 1981.

q.s: Environmental Impact Assessment originated globally with the National Environmental Policy Act of the USA in:
q.x: NEPA (1969) introduced EIA; in India the DST examined river-valley projects from 1976-77 and EIA was first used in 1978.

q.s: The Basel, Rotterdam and Stockholm conventions on hazardous chemicals and wastes share a joint secretariat under:
q.x: The three conventions work together under a 'synergies' arrangement with a joint secretariat administered by UNEP.

q.s: The Stockholm Convention deals with:
o: Prior informed consent for hazardous chemicals
q.x: Stockholm covers POPs; Basel covers hazardous waste movement, Rotterdam prior informed consent and Minamata mercury.

q.s: The Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board was set up in 1976 under the:
o: Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
q.x: APPCB was set up under the Water Act; it now allots inspections through a computerised, risk-based system.

q.s: CCUS, for which the Union Budget 2026 proposed Rs 20,000 crore, stands for:
q.x: CCUS captures CO2 from sources like power and cement plants; DST approved five CCUS test beds in May 2025.

q.s: India's first organic Union Territory is:
q.x: Lakshadweep is the first organic UT and Sikkim the first organic State; Meghalaya and Nagaland also pursue organic status.

q.s: Which of the following North-Eastern States is NOT pursuing organic-State status?
q.x: Sikkim (India's first organic State), Meghalaya and Nagaland are pursuing organic status; Assam is not.

q.s: The south-west monsoon accounts for about what share of India's annual rainfall?
q.x: About 75% of India's rain comes in June-September; the north-east monsoon mainly benefits Tamil Nadu and the south-east coast.

q.s: Which of the following statements about sea-level rise is correct?
o: Thermal expansion and melting of land ice are its principal causes.
Melting of floating sea ice is its principal cause.
The rate of rise has halved since 1901.
The IPCC projects a one-metre rise by 2070.
q.x: Floating ice adds little; the rate has roughly doubled to about 4.5 mm a year, and the IPCC projects about 0.43-0.84 m by 2100.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the 2030 Agenda is correct?
o: It was adopted at Rio de Janeiro in 2015.
The decision to frame the SDGs was taken at Rio+20 in 2012.
It was adopted by the G20.
q.x: Rio+20 decided to frame the SDGs; the UN General Assembly adopted the 2030 Agenda at New York in September 2015, replacing the MDGs (2000-2015).

q.s: The central motto of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development is:
q.x: 'Leave no one behind' is the 2030 Agenda's pledge; 'Only one Earth' was the Stockholm 1972 slogan and 'Our Common Future' the Brundtland Report.

q.s: Which of the following diseases is NOT spread by mosquitoes?
q.x: Cholera is water-borne; JE (Culex), chikungunya and Zika (Aedes) are mosquito-borne.

q.s: India's maternal mortality ratio has fallen since 1990 by about:
q.x: India's MMR has fallen about 86% and under-five mortality about 78% since 1990, while the risk of dying from NCDs has risen among older adults.

q.s: An epidemic disease among animals is called:
q.x: Epizootic means an animal epidemic; endemic means steadily present in a place, and zoonotic means passing from animals to humans.

q.s: As per NFHS-6, households with at least one member covered by health insurance rose from 41.0% to:
q.x: NFHS-6 shows 60.2% of households with an insured member; government-financed insurance coverage rose about 2.5-fold since 2017-18.

q.s: The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) functions under the:
o: Department of Health Research, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
q.x: ICMR, founded in 1911 as the Indian Research Fund Association and renamed in 1949, works under the Department of Health Research.

q.s: National Science Day (28 February) commemorates the discovery of the Raman Effect in the year:
q.x: C.V. Raman announced the Raman Effect on 28 February 1928 and won the Nobel Prize in 1930; National Technology Day (11 May) marks Pokhran-II.

q.s: National Mathematics Day is celebrated on 22 December to mark the birth anniversary of:
q.x: It was declared in 2012, the 125th birth anniversary of Ramanujan.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a consensus mechanism used in blockchain networks?
q.x: Ethereum is a blockchain platform; Proof of Work, Proof of Stake and Proof of Authority are consensus mechanisms.

q.s: Finland has set its target year for carbon neutrality as:
q.x: Finland targets 2035, well ahead of the EU's 2050; it joined the EU in 1995 and is an Arctic Council member.

q.s: The fourth India-Africa Forum Summit (IAFS-IV), planned for New Delhi in May 2026, was postponed because of:
o: The Ebola outbreak in DR Congo and Uganda
A boycott by the African Union
q.x: IAFS-IV was postponed after the WHO declared the Ebola outbreak a Public Health Emergency of International Concern.

q.s: During his February 2026 address in Kuala Lumpur, PM Modi announced that a Thiruvalluvar Chair and Centre would be set up at:
q.x: The Thiruvalluvar Chair is at Universiti Malaya; he also said OCI cards would be extended to the sixth generation of the diaspora.

q.s: India's target of 500 GW of non-fossil fuel based capacity is set for the year:
q.x: The 500 GW target is for 2030; India reached 50% non-fossil installed capacity in July 2025 and targets net zero by 2070.

q.s: The Beijing Declaration and Platform for Action, reviewed at 'Beijing+30', was adopted at the Fourth World Conference on Women in:
q.x: The Beijing conference was held in 1995; Beijing+30 called for universal ratification of CEDAW.

q.s: Which of the following statements about June-August 2026 is correct?
o: India gave USD 2.5 million to UNRWA as the first instalment of its annual USD 5 million.
Sarnath was inscribed as a natural World Heritage Site.
The 48th World Heritage Committee met at New Delhi.
WHO validated El Salvador for eliminating leprosy.
q.x: The 48th Committee met at Busan; Sarnath was inscribed in the cultural category, and El Salvador was validated for eliminating trachoma.

q.s: The Kimberley Process, which India chairs in 2026, aims to prevent trade in:
q.x: The Kimberley Process certifies rough diamonds to stop conflict diamonds; the Colombo Process deals with overseas employment of migrant workers.

q.s: Operation Atalanta, an anti-piracy operation off the Horn of Africa, is run by:
q.x: Operation Atalanta is run by EUNAVFOR; the Windsor Framework (2023) concerns trade between Great Britain and Northern Ireland.

q.s: The Director-General of the WTO, Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, is from:
q.x: Okonjo-Iweala of Nigeria began her second term in September 2025; MC13 was held at Abu Dhabi in 2024.

q.s: Under the WTO Agreement on Agriculture, minimally trade-distorting support that has no limit is placed in the:
q.x: Green Box support has no ceiling; Amber Box support is trade-distorting and subject to limits.

q.s: The CII Partnership Summit is organised by the Confederation of Indian Industry together with:
o: DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
q.x: CII holds the summit every year (since 1995) with DPIIT; the 31st summit's theme began 'Navigating the New World Order'.

q.s: 'Garuda Shakti' is a joint special forces exercise between India and:
q.x: The 11th Garuda Shakti was held at Banyuwangi, East Java; AUSTRAHIND is with Australia.

q.s: The Baghdad Pact, a Cold War defence alliance in West Asia, was signed in:
q.x: The Baghdad Pact dates from 1955; the Arab League Joint Defence Treaty from 1950 and the GCC's Peninsula Shield Force from 1984.

q.s: The International Fleet Review 2026 was held at:
q.x: Visakhapatnam hosted the IFR 2026 (it also hosted the 2016 IFR); the MQ-9B drones India ordered in 2024 are made by General Atomics.

q.s: The Monroe Doctrine of 1823 opposed:
q.x: The Monroe Doctrine opposed European interference in the Americas; the Roosevelt Corollary (1904) expanded it and the Truman Doctrine aimed at Cold War containment.

q.s: IBSAMAR is a trilateral naval exercise among the navies of India, Brazil and:
q.x: IBSAMAR brings together the IBSA countries - India, Brazil and South Africa.

q.s: The Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Centre, known for 3D mapping of the human brain, is at:
q.x: The brain centre is at IIT Madras; IIT Bombay built a low-cost device for anaemia and sickle cell, and IIT Hyderabad hosts the Telangana critical minerals CoE.

q.s: The PM E-DRIVE scheme (2024) for electric mobility is implemented by the Ministry of:
q.x: PM E-DRIVE, the successor of FAME, is run by the Ministry of Heavy Industries; EV adoption rose to 8.26% in FY26.

q.s: An FCEV (Fuel Cell Electric Vehicle) usually runs on:
q.x: FCEVs use a fuel cell, usually hydrogen; a BEV runs on battery only and a PHEV is a hybrid with a plug-in battery.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Matsya-6000 is correct?
o: Its mother ship is Sagar Kanya.
It is an uncrewed robotic vehicle.
It is built by ISRO under the Gaganyaan programme.
It is meant to take three aquanauts to a depth of 6,000 m.
q.x: Matsya-6000, a crewed submersible of the Deep Ocean Mission (Ministry of Earth Sciences), operates from the ship Sagar Nidhi.

q.s: The Chips to Startup (C2S) programme for building semiconductor design talent was launched by:
q.x: MeitY launched C2S in 2022; the DIR-V programme for RISC-V processors was also launched in 2022.

q.s: The universal donor of red blood cells is the blood group:
q.x: O negative cells carry no A, B or Rh(D) antigens; AB positive is the universal recipient and AB the universal plasma donor.

q.s: Nameri National Park, declared in 1998, is in the State of:
q.x: Nameri is in Assam, adjoining Pakke in Arunachal Pradesh; CA|TS (Conservation Assured Tiger Standards) was launched in 2013.

q.s: The Sakurajima volcano is located near:
q.x: Sakurajima is near Kagoshima; Semeru is Java's highest peak and Santiaguito is in Guatemala.

q.s: The International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA) was launched in April 2023 to mark 50 years of:
q.x: IBCA was launched on 9 April 2023; it covers seven big cats, including the puma and jaguar, and is headquartered in India.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the seven big cats covered by the International Big Cat Alliance?
q.x: The seven are tiger, lion, leopard, snow leopard, cheetah, jaguar and puma.

q.s: The National Innovations in Climate Resilient Agriculture (NICRA) project is run by:
q.x: NICRA, covering 651 districts, is an ICAR project; India was 9th worst-hit for 1995-2024 in the Climate Risk Index 2026.

q.s: According to WWF's Living Planet Report 2024, the steepest decline in monitored wildlife populations was in the:
q.x: Freshwater populations fell 85% and marine 56%; the overall average decline was 73% (1970-2020).

q.s: Which Indian museum was ranked 9th in the world, and first in Asia, in the 'World's 100 Best Museums' list of 2026?
q.x: Bihar Museum was 9th; Golconda Fort was the 7th most-visited ticketed ASI monument in 2025-26.

q.s: ULLAS, under which States are declared fully literate, stands for:
o: Universal Literacy and Learning for Adult Students
Understanding of Lifelong Learning for All in Society
q.x: Under ULLAS-Nav Bharat Saaksharta Karyakram, Ladakh was declared fully literate in 2024 and Uttarakhand became the sixth fully literate State.

q.s: The World Investment Report is published by:
q.x: UNCTAD publishes the World Investment Report; in 2025 India received USD 38.89 bn of FDI, ranking 11th.

q.s: According to the IFI 2026 report, which State accounts for about 31% of India's merchandise exports?
q.x: Gujarat leads merchandise exports and Maharashtra has 35% of PE/VC investment; the North-East gets less than 1% of FDI.

q.s: As of 30 June 2026, non-fossil sources made up about what share of India's installed power capacity?
q.x: Non-fossil sources reached 54.18%, beyond the NDC target of 50% by 2030; RE capacity was about 288.58 GW.

q.s: According to UNEP, the second most consumed material in the world after water is:
q.x: UNEP calls sand the second most consumed material; global forest cover fell from 4.18 bn ha (2015) to 4.14 bn ha (2025).

q.s: In the Global Firepower Index 2026, India was ranked:
q.x: The USA, Russia and China were the top three and India fourth; Pakistan was 14th.

q.s: The World Drug Report is published by:
q.x: UNODC publishes the World Drug Report; the Global Wage Report is by the ILO and the International Migration Outlook by the OECD.

q.s: The Global Wage Report is released by the:
q.x: The ILO publishes the Global Wage Report; UN DESA publishes the World Economic Situation and Prospects.

q.s: The first recipient of the Jnanpith Award (1965) was:
q.x: G. Sankara Kurup (Malayalam) received the first award; Viswanatha Satyanarayana (1970) was the first Telugu recipient.

q.s: The first Telugu writer to receive the Jnanpith Award was:
q.x: Viswanatha received it in 1970 for 'Ramayana Kalpavrukshamu'; C. Narayana Reddy (1988) and Ravuri Bharadwaja (2012) followed.

q.s: The Indian-origin climate scientist Veerabhadran Ramanathan received which international honour in 2026?
q.x: Ramanathan won the Crawford Prize; Srinivas Kulkarni received the RAS Gold Medal.

q.s: The Dronacharya Award, instituted in 1985, is given to:
q.x: Dronacharya honours coaches; the Dhyan Chand Award is the lifetime award for sportspersons.

q.s: The final of the FIFA World Cup 2026 was played at:
q.x: The final was at MetLife Stadium, where Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time; the opening match was at Estadio Azteca.

q.s: Which country won the FIFA World Cup 2026?
q.x: Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time with a goal by Ferran Torres.

q.s: India's first World Rowing Cup gold, won by Army rowers Lakshya and Ujwal Kumar Singh in 2026, came at:
q.x: They won the lightweight men's double sculls at Lucerne; India also topped the ISSF Junior World Championship at Suhl.

q.s: Para shooting is to move to the ISSF from which body before the LA Paralympics 2028?
q.x: Para shooting will move from the IPC to the ISSF; India topped the ISSF Junior World Cup in Cairo with 16 medals.

q.s: The inaugural Deaf Cricket Asia Cup, won by India in 2026, was held at:
q.x: India won the first Deaf Cricket Asia Cup at Cuttack; India-A women won the Asia Cup Rising Stars against Bangladesh-A.

q.s: Which team won the Women's Premier League (WPL) 2026, its second title, under Smriti Mandhana?
q.x: RCB won their second title; Delhi Capitals lost their fourth consecutive final.

q.s: The first BRIC Summit was held in 2009 at:
q.x: The first BRIC Summit was at Yekaterinburg, Russia; India holds the BRICS Chairship in 2026 after Brazil (2025).

q.s: Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment) was launched in October 2022 at:
q.x: PM Modi and the UN Secretary-General launched Mission LiFE at Kevadia on 20 October 2022; the idea had been announced at COP26.

q.s: International Translation Day is observed on:
q.x: It falls on 30 September, the feast of St Jerome; UN Disarmament Week begins on UN Day, 24 October, and World Rivers Day is the fourth Sunday of September.

q.s: 'Cyber Sarathi', launched in Telangana in 2026, is:
o: The first AI voice agent for cybercrime complaints on 1930
q.x: Cyber Sarathi handles 1930 cybercrime complaints; Telangana's Operation Crackdown targets mule accounts.

q.s: The Konark Sun Temple was built around 1250 CE by the Eastern Ganga king:
q.x: Narasimhadeva I built Konark; its Jagamohan, filled with sand by the British in 1903-04, was reopened in 2026.

q.s: Bhirrana, an Indus Valley settlement that may date back about 8,000 years, is in which State?
q.x: Bhirrana is in Fatehabad district, Haryana.

q.s: Which of the following statements about swadeshi ideas is correct?
o: Dadabhai Naoroji put forward the Drain of Wealth theory.
M.G. Ranade opposed the use of domestic goods.
R.C. Dutt wrote 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'.
q.x: Naoroji wrote 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'; Ranade urged preferring domestic goods even if costlier, and R.C. Dutt wrote 'The Economic History of India'.

q.s: P.N. Panicker, the subject of P.P. Sathyan's book 'The Library Man of India', led the library movement in:
q.x: P.N. Panicker is the father of the library movement in Kerala; Bhawaiya is folk music of North Bengal and Assam.

q.s: Who became the first woman Indian Army officer to serve as ADC to the President in 2026?
q.x: Major Navya Shekhawat became the President's first woman Army ADC; Bhawana Kanth was the first woman to complete the IAF Fighter Combat Leader course.

q.s: India's envoy to a Commonwealth country such as New Zealand is designated as:
q.x: India sends High Commissioners to Commonwealth countries and Ambassadors to others.

q.s: The Inter-State Council under Article 263 is chaired by the:
q.x: The Inter-State Council, set up in 1990 on the Sarkaria Commission's advice, is chaired by the Prime Minister.

q.s: The retirement age of High Court judges (62 years) is laid down in:
q.x: Article 217 fixes 62 for High Court judges; Article 124 fixes 65 for Supreme Court judges and Article 213 gives the Governor's ordinance power.

q.s: The Governor's power to promulgate ordinances is provided under:
q.x: Article 213 deals with the Governor's ordinances; Article 123 with the President's.

q.s: In ADR v. Election Commission of India, the Supreme Court held that doubtful citizenship cases found during roll revision must go to:
o: The Central Government under the Citizenship Act, 1955
The Election Commission for final decision
q.x: The Court upheld the SIR order for Bihar but held that the ECI can only look at citizenship prima facie; final decisions lie with the Central Government.

q.s: In State of Andhra Pradesh vs Suda Suresh Veera Venkata Naga Raju, the Supreme Court held that the total period of police custody of an accused cannot exceed:
q.x: Custody may be sought in parts during the first 40 or 60 days, but the total stays capped at 15 days.

q.s: The meaning of 'industry' under the Industrial Disputes Act, now being re-examined by a nine-judge Bench, was laid down in 1978 in:
o: Minerva Mills v. Union of India
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
Bangalore Water Supply v. A. Rajappa
q.x: The 1978 seven-judge ruling, with the majority opinion by Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer, gave the Triple Test under which profit motive and capital are irrelevant.

q.s: Under the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950, persons of which religion are NOT eligible for Scheduled Caste status?
q.x: Clause 3 of the Order limits SC status to Hindus, Sikhs (added 1956) and Buddhists (added 1990).

q.s: The freeze on the inter-State allocation of Lok Sabha seats, based on the 1971 Census, was extended till the first Census after 2026 by the:
q.x: The 42nd Amendment first froze the allocation and the 84th Amendment extended it; the 2002-08 Delimitation Commission only redrew internal boundaries.

q.s: A writ petition under Article 32 can be filed in the Supreme Court only for the violation of:
q.x: Article 32 is a remedy for fundamental rights only; High Courts under Article 226 can also enforce ordinary legal rights.

q.s: Which of the following statements about parliamentary privileges is correct?
o: Freedom from arrest covers only civil cases.
Freedom from arrest extends to criminal cases.
Freedom from arrest covers preventive detention.
The press may publish reports of secret sittings.
q.x: Members are free from civil arrest during a session and 40 days before and after; the 44th Amendment protects fair reporting of proceedings but not of secret sittings.

q.s: BMI, which raised its 2026 growth forecast for India to 7.5%, is a division of:
q.x: BMI is part of Fitch Solutions; the 7.4% projection for India in 2026 came from the IMF.

q.s: CORSIA, the scheme for carbon-neutral growth of international aviation, was adopted by:
q.x: CORSIA is ICAO's Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation; India now allows ethanol and synthetic hydrocarbons in ATF.

q.s: India's two Defence Industrial Corridors are located in:
q.x: The corridors are in UP and Tamil Nadu; India has been the second-largest steel producer since 2018.

q.s: The first flight under the UDAN regional connectivity scheme was between:
q.x: UDAN was launched on 21 October 2016 and its first flight was Shimla-Delhi in April 2017.

q.s: With which country did India record its largest bilateral trade deficit in 2025?
q.x: India's trade deficit with China hit a record of about USD 116 billion in 2025; India ranked 7th in data-centre investments.

q.s: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana provides free electricity of up to how many units a month through rooftop solar?
q.x: The MNRE scheme (February 2024) targets 1 crore households with up to 300 free units and a subsidy of up to Rs 78,000.

q.s: Under PMAY-Gramin, the assistance per house in plain areas is:
q.x: PMAY-G gives Rs 1.20 lakh in plains and Rs 1.30 lakh in hilly areas; PMAY-U 2.0 gives up to Rs 2.5 lakh under Beneficiary-Led Construction.

q.s: The Amrit Bharat Station Scheme of the Indian Railways aims at:
q.x: It covers redevelopment of 1,338 stations; AMRUT 2.0 covers all 4,800 statutory towns.

q.s: Tele-MANAS, part of India's policy response to mental health, is a:
q.x: Tele-MANAS offers round-the-clock tele-counselling; the National Mental Health Survey found 7-10% of adolescents with diagnosable conditions.

q.s: The NAMASTE scheme, implemented through NSKFDC, is meant for:
q.x: NAMASTE covers sewer, septic tank and waste-picker workers; PM VIKAS is for minorities and the Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana for senior citizens.

q.s: Which of the following statements about malaria is correct?
o: Malaria cases in the Asia-Pacific rose in 2024.
India targets zero indigenous cases by 2035.
Malaria is caused by a virus.
q.x: India aims at zero indigenous cases by 2027 and elimination by 2030; Asia-Pacific cases fell from 9.6 million (2023) to 8.9 million (2024). Malaria is caused by Plasmodium, a protozoan.
